hard_parts: Tablet objects hold pointers into themselves. ObTablet::deserialize deep-copies read info, table store, the ddl_kvs array and macro info into the bytes after sizeof(ObTablet) inside a fixed pool buffer (3,824 B or 65,480 B), with a bitfield header before the object found by pointer arithmetic. Paths: src/storage/tablet/ob_tablet.cpp:1663-1815; src/storage/meta_mem/ob_storage_meta_obj_pool.h:41-110.

Tablet wash under memory pressure. The pool asks the manager for a free buffer by std::type_info; the manager evicts a cold tablet whose refcount is 0 and hands the raw buffer over, while ObTabletPointer keeps the disk address so the tablet can be loaded again. Path: src/storage/meta_mem/ob_storage_meta_mem_mgr.cpp:2137-2200.

Hand-rolled ref-counted guards and handles: ObMetaObjGuard<T> copy/assign with inc_ref/dec_ref, freed either to an object pool or through allocator plus explicit destructor, with runtime leak and threading checks. ObTabletHandle, ObTableHandleV2 and ObLSHandle appear on 1,122 lines in 186 files. Path: src/storage/meta_mem/ob_meta_obj_struct.h:160-385.

The memtable B-tree ObKeyBtree: templates over key/value, a union-packed spin RWLock, retire lists and QClock deferred reclamation from oblib, and a .cpp included textually into its header. Paths: src/storage/memtable/mvcc/ob_keybtree.cpp, ob_keybtree.h:328, ob_keybtree_deps.h:61-105 and 407-432.

Intrusive MVCC structures: ObMvccTransNode has raw prev_/next_ pointers, a zero-length trailing buffer and CAS-set flag bits. Nodes come from the memstore arena (ObFifoArena: bump pages with atomic ref and pos) and are linked into both the row chain and the transaction callback list. Paths: src/storage/memtable/mvcc/ob_mvcc_row.h:63-95, src/storage/memtable/mvcc/ob_tx_callback_list.cpp, src/storage/allocator/ob_fifo_arena.h:43-190.

On-disk headers that are packed memory images with bitfields and unions:
- ObMicroBlockHeader: a 64-byte image whose pointer shares a union with an int64;
- ObMacroBlockCommonHeader, ObSSTableMacroBlockHeader::FixedHeader and 13 encoder meta headers.
A byte-exact Rust codec must reproduce GCC/Clang bitfield ordering explicitly. Paths: src/storage/blocksstable/ob_micro_block_header.h, ob_sstable_macro_block_header.cpp:162-230, encoding/*_encoder.h.

Encoding styles differ within the same file set: little-endian memory images, big-endian encode_iN (oblib serialization.h:212), unis varint with version/length envelopes, and SERIALIZE_MEMBER_WITH_MEMCPY. The stored cell bytes are ObDatum payloads (ob_row_writer.cpp:666-688), so a Rust engine must also reproduce oblib's ObNumber, decimal and datetime byte layouts.

KV-cache pointer swizzling: the index block row scanner keeps raw pointers into cache memory blocks, checked by version and hazard version. Paths: src/storage/blocksstable/ob_kvcache_pointer_swizzle.{h,cpp}; src/share/cache/ob_kvcache_hazard_version.h.

Encoders and decoders are dispatched through template-generated N-dimensional function-pointer tables filled at static-init time. SIMD kernels are template specializations behind #if __AVX512BW__ and NEON variants, and they take sql::PushdownFilterInfo and sql::ObBitVector. Paths: src/storage/blocksstable/encoding/ob_dict_decoder.cpp:128-182, ob_encoding_query_util.h:225-260, ob_raw_decoder_simd.cpp, neon/.

The read path is tied to the SQL expression engine: access and blocksstable take sql::ObPushdownFilterExecutor, ObEvalCtx, ObExpr and ObBitVector (1,069 sql:: lines). The read path cannot be moved without either keeping those C++ types across FFI or moving the pushdown and expression layer too. Paths: src/storage/access/ob_pushdown_aggregate.cpp, src/storage/blocksstable/encoding/*_decoder.cpp.

Borrowed row views flow through deep iterator chains. ObDatum and ObStorageDatum point into micro-block buffers pinned by cache handles, through ObMultipleMerge -> sstable row scanner -> micro block row scanner -> decoder. The pin/view lifetime is an unwritten rule that Rust would have to state as lifetimes or turn into copies. Paths: src/storage/access/ob_multiple_merge.cpp, src/storage/blocksstable/ob_micro_block_row_scanner.cpp.

Two-phase init and error-code style: is_inited_ on 2,841 lines in 551 files, and OB_FAIL on 16,267 lines. Mechanically this maps to constructors and Result, but the sheer volume makes it the bulk of the translation effort (all directories).
pain_instances: 9e2b6ba16 (2026-01-22), src/storage/ddl/ob_tablet_fork_task.cpp. A stack-local ObTableStoreIterator pinned the sstables, but the raw sstable pointers collected from it (src_sstables) were used after it went out of scope. The fix moved the iterator into the long-lived context. A borrow checker rejects a reference that outlives the value it borrows from.

62b9d1a81 (2025-11-04), src/storage/ddl/ob_ddl_independent_dag.cpp: 'fix mem leak due to parallel using mem'. A single ObArenaAllocator (not thread-safe) was shared by parallel merge tasks. The fix swapped in a FIFO allocator and added manual tracking with destructor-then-free for each merge helper. Rust's Send/Sync would have refused the sharing, and Drop would handle the cleanup.

9bb15300f (2025-12-04), src/storage/ddl/ob_hnsw_embedmgr.cpp: '[CP] core fix'. The slot ring called ~ObEmbeddingTask() and ob_free while the embedding handler thread could still hold the task. The fix added manual retain_if_managed/release_if_managed refcounting, which is what an Arc gives by construction.

37b91155c (2025-11-10), src/storage/ddl/ob_ddl_tablet_context.{h,cpp} and ob_ddl_merge_task_v2.cpp: 'fix bug, fix core'. The merge helper's owner was unclear: it was created per task parameter inside a dag arena. The fix moved ownership into MergeCtx with an explicit destructor call and an is_inited_ guard.

b7abb6324 (2026-04-21), src/storage/memtable/ob_nop_bitmap.h: 'fix hung and core when drop column'. `~0LU`, `1LU << pos` and __builtin_ctzl were 32-bit under Windows LLP64 and corrupted the upper 32 bits of a 64-bit bitmap. Rust's fixed-width u64 and trailing_zeros remove that whole class of bug.

b8eafbae8 (2026-01-29) and 3dc21147b (2026-01-26), src/storage/access/ob_multiple_merge.cpp. A hash map that was not yet created (extra_access_ctx_) was queried, returning OB_NOT_INIT, and the refresh code built it in the wrong order. This is the two-phase-init state problem that an Option<HashMap> would force the code to handle.

CI runs 283 mysqltest .test files from tools/deploy/mysql_test: 93 in t/ and 190 in test_suite/*/t, selected by .github/script/seekdb/mysqltest_for_seekdb.py:248-272. Every DML and SELECT test goes through storage-core (ObAccessService -> ObLSTabletService -> memtable or access), but most tests keep their data in the memtable.

Tests that reach deeper paths:
- 11 run 'alter system major/minor freeze' (13 statements of each), which drive the sstable writer, compaction and the merge read path. survey.units_of_work:
File level: 649 .h/.cpp basenames (553 pairs, 94 header-only, 2 triples) in 37 leaf directories. Because of the coupling, the units that can realistically be translated and tested on their own are 12 directory groups (lines in brackets):
1. On-disk block formats and readers/writers: blocksstable including encoding and index_block, 235 files [87,627].
2. Tablet metadata and persistence: tablet + meta_mem + meta_store + slog + slog_ckpt + blockstore + truncate_info [63,369].
3. Memtable/MVCC with its allocators: memtable + allocator + throttle [30,932].
4. Read path: access [32,058], blocked on the query-layer pushdown types.
5. Compaction plus dag scheduler: compaction + scheduler [39,411].
6. DDL data paths: ddl [34,344].
7. LOB: lob [14,210].
8. Temp files: tmp_file [20,893].
9. LS container and services: ls + tx_storage + checkpoint [25,791].
10. Tx-adjacent: tx_table + deadlock + concurrency_control [15,137].
11. Search/vector: retrieval + vector_type + vector_index [14,393].
12. Root files: ob_i_table, ob_storage_schema, ob_storage_struct, DML context and similar [27,420].
Groups 1-3 are the redesign core and must come first; groups 4-9 depend on them. Dead files (4,028 lines) drop out.
open_questions: Must a Rust engine read existing seekdb data directories at all? Two persisted enums were renumbered after v1.1.0 (1a6192cf6, 4238c88e9) with no mapping code, and no upgrade or format-compatibility policy was found in docs/. The project owners have to answer this; it decides whether the four encoding styles must be reproduced byte for byte.

Are data files byte-identical between Linux (clang, Itanium ABI) and Windows (clang-cl, MSVC ABI) builds, given the packed bitfield headers? This needs a cross-platform dump comparison and cannot be settled read-only.

What does it cost to keep the storage/SQL seam as FFI? data_plane/api (16,157 lines, another area) exports C++ value types such as ObDatumRow, ObStorageDatum and ObTableScanParam carrying sql::ObExpr pointers, not just abstract interfaces. The size of the actual call surface was not measured.
How often does tablet wash or GC actually run in embedded mode, and how much of the pooled-buffer design is needed for single-node sizes? This needs a running instance with metrics.
Is there any performance baseline for the AVX-512/NEON decoder filters and the keybtree? No storage benchmarks are tracked, so a rewrite has no reference numbers to match.
Can any of the 500 cluster-era obtest scripts (storage, minor_freeze, errsim_storage) be adapted to single-node seekdb to cover restart/replay and compaction? This was not tried.

Whether tx_table, tx_storage, deadlock and concurrency_control (24,380 lines together, tx-adjacent) and retrieval/vector (14,393) should count here or with the tx and fts researchers. This report counts them in storage-core per the literal area definition.

checks.corrected: The micro block header is written as the raw memory image of a packed 64-byte struct with bitfields and anonymous unions. The last 8 bytes are a union of `int64_t *column_checksums_` and `min_merged_trans_version_`. When has_column_checksum_ is set, serialize (via deep_copy) writes nullptr there and deserialize points column_checksums_ into the input buffer. When has_min_merged_trans_version_ is set, the slot carries the real min_merged_trans_version_ on disk.

Read ob_storage_meta_mem_mgr.cpp:2061-2220. try_wash_tablet takes a std::type_info and compares it to typeid(ObNormalTabletBuffer/ObLargeTabletBuffer). I agree with 'Split', and the redesign-core file list is right: ob_tablet.cpp:1670-1815 (self-referencing pooled buffer), ob_storage_meta_mem_mgr.cpp:2137-2220 (wash chosen by type_info), ob_meta_obj_struct.h (hand-rolled guards), the keybtree files and ob_micro_block_header.cpp all show code that safe Rust cannot express one-to-one. (2) The error style does not map purely onto Result and `?`. verification.overall: The survey's counts and code citations are reliable. The size split reproduces to the line, every file:line I opened matched the claim, and all the cited commits say what the survey says they say. Its errors are in a few places. First, some counts depend on the regex (lock guards and bucket locks are undercounted about 2x, and multiple inheritance about 2x). Second, a few conclusions go further than the evidence. 3e877d774 does not break v1.1.0 compatibility, although the LZ4 removal makes the compatibility break stronger than stated. 'Only three outside callers' ignores the data_plane/api seam that SQL actually uses. And CI runs 272 configured tests, not all 283, which drops 3 freeze tests and the only storage fault-injection test. There is also one arithmetic slip (23,380, not 24,380). The main technical claims survive checking: the packed-image on-disk headers, the tablets that hold pointers into their own buffers, the hand-rolled guards, the keybtree reclamation (two mechanisms, not one), and the SQL-type coupling in the read path. The 'Split' structure call is sound, but it understates how far the handles, the global service registry and the tx/MDS dependencies reach into the 'easy' half. Use its numbers as given; treat its compatibility and test-coverage conclusions as needing the corrections above.

survey.what_it_is: This area is seekdb's single-node transaction engine and its write-ahead log. survey.summary:
1. This area is 131,673 hand-written lines in 493 files, with no generated or vendored code. It is shrinking fast as distributed features are pruned: tx went from 75,472 lines at v1.0.0 to 37,512 at HEAD, and logservice from 84,064 to 32,705.
2. The transaction model is a single-node, one-phase commit. commit_version = max(local gts, max_read_ts+1) is passed to the log append, then overwritten with the SCN (commit timestamp) of the TX_COMMIT_LOG itself.
3. Only REDO_COMPLETE, COMMIT and ABORT are ever set as durable states. MVCC visibility comes from ObTxData (state, commit_version, undo ranges) held in the tx table, and from memtable version backfill.
4. palf-lite is a local write-ahead log where commit means the local flush finished. Election, reconfiguration and network code are gone.
5. Recovery starts palf in a RECOVERING state, then replays from base_lsn. Replay is split into queues by replay_hint − tx_id, into 32 replay queues and 64 apply queues.
6. A checkpoint takes the minimum rec_scn (recovery start SCN) reported by roughly 10 checkpoint handlers, then advances base_lsn.
7. The core is hard to port as a one-to-one translation. ObTxCtx is a 6,113-line .cpp with 174 methods and three latches, and it holds the memtable context by value. Its log callbacks form an intrusive, reference-counted cycle with the apply service, with ob_abort() enforcing the order in which callbacks complete.
8. MDS is compile-time metaprogramming: an X-macro header included at 11 sites, including inside an enum body, plus template tuple-index recursion.
9. On-disk compatibility is weaker than assumed. The project itself broke clog and ctx-table compatibility after v1.1.0: LogGroupEntryHeader now accepts only version 3, and the tx log and exec-info field lists were pruned. HEAD's format definitions match v1.4.0 (tagged 2026-08-26), so v1.4.0 is the realistic compatibility baseline, if one is required at all.
10. Standby makes the palf group-entry bytes a wire format as well.
11. For verification, the in-tree unit tests for this area were deleted in 45cbbe9e1. CI runs 272 mysqltest cases, about 21 of them transaction-focused, and none restarts the server, so replay and recovery have no in-repo CI coverage.
12. Recent transaction bug fixes are mostly protocol, ordering or logic errors that Rust would not have prevented. The defensive code, though (manual refcount aborts, spin-waits for references to drop, two-phase init checks), is the kind Rust ownership removes.

survey.structure_call:
This area splits into two parts.

**Parts that can be translated keeping their structure:**
- The byte formats: palf block, group and entry headers, LogMeta, ObLogBaseHeader, the tx log block and bodies, ObTxExecInfo and ObTxData rows, ObPresistIDLog, and the UNIS encoding with positional fields and placeholder fields that must stay in place.
- palf-lite's single-writer pipeline (LSN allocator, then group buffer, then one IO thread, then flush callback), and the apply and replay services.
- These are either byte contracts or local pipelines with simple ownership. They map to Rust structs with derived encode/decode code. The 128-bit CAS needs a small unsafe or portable-atomic island.

**Parts where idiomatic Rust forces a redesign:**
- The transaction core. ObTxCtx inherits from both ObTransCtx and ObLink. It holds the memtable context by value and keeps an intrusive list of ObTxLogCb objects that hold raw ObTxCtx* pointers. The apply service reaches those callbacks through AppendCb intrusive links (CONTAINER_OF). Lifetimes are enforced by manual reference counts, and the lock protocol hands locks off through before_unlock/after_unlock.
- MDS, which is X-macro and template metaprogramming with no one-to-one Rust form.
- The tablelock object-lock map with intrusive lists and priority queues, a moderate redesign.
- A literal translation would be raw pointers and unsafe code throughout. The natural Rust design is an Arc'd context with state split across separate locks, completion events delivered in submit order through a channel or sequence number, and an enum plus trait registry for MDS types.
- The transaction core cannot be cut out alone: memtable (27K lines) and tx_table (10K lines) move with it.
- data_plane (ObITransactionService, 26 methods) is the ready-made trait or FFI boundary on the SQL side.

**Committed line:** redesign is forced by src/storage/tx/ob_tx_ctx.{h,cpp}, src/storage/tx/ob_trans_submit_log_cb.h and src/logservice/ob_append_callback.{h,cpp} (the ownership cycle between the transaction context, its log callbacks and the memtable, held together by manual reference counts), and by src/storage/multi_data_source/compile_utility/{mds_register.h,compile_mapper.h} and src/storage/multi_data_source/mds_node.h (X-macro and template metaprogramming). The formats in src/storage/tx/ob_tx_log.{h,cpp} and src/logservice/palf/log_*_header.cpp can be translated keeping their structure.
hard_parts: Ownership cycle between transaction contexts and log callbacks. ObTxCtx (src/storage/tx/ob_tx_ctx.h:103) inherits ObTransCtx (an ObLightHashLink reference count, src/storage/tx/ob_trans_ctx.h:85) and ObLink. It owns common::ObDList<ObTxLogCb> busy_cbs_ (ob_tx_ctx.h:633). Each ObTxLogCb holds a raw ObTxCtx* (src/storage/tx/ob_trans_submit_log_cb.h:83-130) and is also queued in the apply service through AppendCb's intrusive __next_ link, recovered with CONTAINER_OF (src/logservice/ob_append_callback.cpp:25).

ObTxCtx is one very large class: ob_tx_ctx.cpp has 6,113 lines and 174 method definitions, plus 5 more in ob_tx_ctx_log_cb_helper.cpp. It holds memtable::ObMemtableCtx by value (ob_tx_ctx.h:598), so transactions and the memtable must be ported together.

Three-latch lock protocol with bitmask modes and lock handoff. CtxLock and CtxLockGuard are in src/storage/tx/ob_trans_ctx_lock.h:62-142. before_unlock/after_unlock with CtxLockArg (ob_trans_ctx.h:131-132) run the commit callback outside the lock. on_success chooses the lock mode dynamically (ob_tx_ctx.cpp:1550).
The ObTransService class body is spread across three headers through #include inside the class (src/storage/tx/ob_trans_service.h:169 and ob_trans_service_v4.h:226).

MDS metaprogramming. The X-macro registry src/storage/multi_data_source/compile_utility/mds_register.h is included at 11 sites, one inside an enum body (src/storage/tx/ob_multi_data_source.h:62-66). compile_mapper.h does type-to-ID mapping and constexpr recursion over tuple indexes. mds_register.h documents detection of optional methods (on_redo, on_commit and others). UserMdsNode uses multiple inheritance whose order must not change (src/storage/multi_data_source/mds_node.h:181, 'this order can not be changed!!!'). MDS has 501 template lines.

Lock-free LSN and SCN allocation: a 128-bit CAS on a bitfield union (src/logservice/palf/lsn_allocator.h:91-99, CAS128 at 8 sites in lsn_allocator.cpp). Rust has no stable AtomicU128, so this needs portable-atomic or inline assembly, or a redesign now that there is a single writer.
FixedSlidingWindow allocates a raw array through ge_alloc, constructs slots with placement new, and gives each slot a reference count and an ObByteLock (src/logservice/palf/fixed_sliding_window.h).

Custom slice allocator: ObTxData and ObUndoStatusNode live in fixed 128-byte slices with embedded hash and sort links, a static_assert on size, and a _WIN32 ABI branch (src/storage/tx/ob_tx_data_define.h:55-112, 369).

Byte-exact positional serialization through OB_SERIALIZE_MEMBER, OB_UNIS_VERSION and DEFINE_SERIALIZE (258 macro lines in the area). Placeholder fields must keep their position: checksum_[0] and checksum_scn_[0] marked 'FARM COMPAT WHITELIST' (src/storage/tx/ob_trans_define.cpp:407-408) and obsolete_trace_payload_ (ob_tx_log.cpp:218). A header field is fixed-size and back-patched through FixSizeTrait_int64_t (ob_tx_log.h:644-692). The redo body is the memtable mutator format, which belongs to storage/memtable.

Type-erased callback arguments: ObTxCbArg holds const void *arg_ (src/storage/tx/ob_tx_log.h, ObTxCbArg). The area has 334 lines mentioning void*, 70 reinterpret_cast and 107 static_cast to pointer types.

Hand-written reference counting in 65 call sites, with guard classes and ob_abort on bad counts (src/storage/tx/ob_tx_data_define.h:375-393, src/logservice/replayservice/ob_replay_status.h:523-637, src/logservice/applyservice/ob_log_apply_service.cpp).

Error-code control flow: 2,248 functions start with 'int ret = OB_SUCCESS', there are 3,628 OB_FAIL/MDS_FAIL, and long if/else-if chains with FALSE_IT side effects (for example ob_tx_ctx.cpp:5687-5712). OB_EAGAIN-driven retry loops appear 239 times.

Direct IO and a pool of preallocated log block files, with platform branches: 125 hits for O_DIRECT, fsync, fallocate, pwrite or pread; 25 _WIN32 and 9 __APPLE__ ifdefs (src/logservice/ob_server_log_block_mgr.cpp, palf/log_block_handler.cpp, palf/log_io_adapter.cpp).

Standby's gRPC service is built on 12,345 lines of generated C++ protobuf code (src/oblib/grpc/standbyservice*.pb.*). It sends serialized ObLSMetaPackage and ObCopyTabletInfo inside protobuf bytes fields (standbyservice.proto:26-31).
pain_instances: src/storage/tx/ob_tx_api.cpp:159-198: ObTransService::reuse_tx waits in a spin loop, with usleep(2000000) per iteration past 2,000 spins, for ObTxDesc's reference count to fall to 1 or 2 before reinitializing it, and calls ob_abort in debug builds after 2,300 spins. This waits out references at run time; unique ownership (Arc::try_unwrap or moving the value) would make it a compile-time property.

src/storage/tx/ob_tx_data_define.cpp:393-394 ('TODO : @gengli remove ob_abort'), 476 and 751, and ob_tx_data_define.h:389: ObTxData and ObTxDataOp crash the process on an invalid reference count or on reset while still referenced. This is defensive code for manual reference counting that Arc/Drop removes.

src/storage/tx/ob_tx_ctx.cpp:2008-2013: on_failure calls ob_abort() when a log callback's cb_arg_array is empty. src/storage/tx/ob_tx_ctx.cpp:3143-3144 calls ob_abort() when log_cb->set_callbacks fails, which is an allocation failure.

src/storage/tx/ob_tx_ctx_mds.cpp:177-195: ObTxMDSCache::is_mem_leak keeps a memory-statistics hash in debug builds to catch leaked MDS nodes. src/storage/multi_data_source/mds_table_mgr.h:37 has RemovedMdsTableRecorder ('tablet leak will resulting mds table leak, we must prove it'). a87fd9832 changed MDS recycle timers from static TG ids to per-instance ids in a service that also kept a memory_leak_debug_map_, which is no longer in HEAD.
src/logservice/palf/palf_handle.h:45-48: the copy-assignment operator is documented to leak PalfHandleImpl and Callback when the target is valid. That is an ownership rule left to comments.

3175abf03 (src/storage/multi_data_source/runtime_utility/mds_factory.cpp): during template recursion over the tuple, deep_copy_buffer_ctx compared the tuple index IDX with old_ctx.get_binding_type_id(), mixing two ID spaces, so the matching context was never copied and new_ctx stayed null. A Rust enum match makes this mistake impossible.

7bef5aa47 (src/logservice/ob_log_service.cpp): a crash in embedded mode caused by a service being skipped at start() yet used later. The area has 1,074 IS_NOT_INIT, OB_INIT_TWICE or is_inited_ checks guarding the two-phase init/start/stop/wait/destroy lifecycle that constructor-based Rust types avoid.

src/storage/multi_data_source/runtime_utility/common_define.h:45-53: MDS_ASSERT calls ob_abort() in release builds, with 62 uses. The area has 34 direct ob_abort() calls in all, many guarding pointer or ordering invariants.
survey.public_surface_tests:
**CI (in-repo, public surface):**
- .github/workflows/seekdb.yml runs mysqltest through .github/script/seekdb/mysqltest_for_seekdb.py over the 272-entry test-set in tools/deploy/mysqltest_config.yaml.
- About 21 of those cases are transaction-focused by name:
  - big_trans_with_mutil_redo, ddlrollback, ms_lose_rollback, sfu, sfu_norow_alias, trans_ac
  - trx_4, trx_5, trx_6, trx_timeout, trx_timeout_bug
  - deadlock_detector.trans_deadlock_basic, executor.trx, fork_table.fork_table_lock, histogram.stats_lock_and_unlock, system_variable.autocommit
  - trx.bug_different_tranid_intrx, trx.repeatable_read_transaction, trx.serializable_constrains, trx.serializable_transaction, trx.trans_weak_read
- 43 of the 283 tools/deploy/mysql_test .test files mention savepoint, rollback, begin/start transaction, lock table, for update or autocommit.
- Every DML test implicitly exercises commit, redo logging, palf append and the apply path.
- No CI mysqltest restarts the server. The config_reboot_value.inc include is empty. Replay, recovery, checkpoint and base_lsn recycling therefore have no in-repo CI coverage.

**Tests that import internals:**
- None at HEAD. Commit 45cbbe9e1 deleted all unittest/ and mittest/ sources, 34 of which (6,642 lines) were unittests for tx, tablelock, MDS, tx_table and logservice.
- A port can therefore be verified only through SQL-level tests and whatever new harness it adds.

**obtest:**
- tools/obtest/t holds 500 .test files, including suites trans (32), trx_succ (10), logservice (4), clog (2) and primary_standby (145).
- 162 of those files stop or restart servers (force_stop or nstart).
- obtest is not wired into CI (git grep obtest -- .github finds nothing), and it is OceanBase-era: 173 cases use CREATE TENANT or multi-zone clusters. For example, tools/obtest/t/logservice/1001_c1_restart_check_data_loss.test queries __all_tenant.

**Outside this repo:**
- Commit messages for 61a371a65 and 370ce4fff point to transaction regression tests in an external repo, seekdb_test (MRs !67, !71, !74).
- Those tests drive debug-sync injection points such as DEBUG_SYNC(BEFORE_TX_ABORT_DECISION) at ob_tx_ctx.cpp:1599. The area has 64 debug-sync or errsim mentions, 19 of them ERRSIM_POINT_DEF.
- A port would have to keep these named hooks for those tests to keep working.
survey.units_of_work:
The natural unit is a file group built around one class family, usually a .h/.cpp pair plus its helpers. The area has 320 file stems in all (tx 57, tablelock 19, MDS 36, palf 51, apply and replay 4, logservice glue 11, standby 28, data_plane 114 headers). That gives about 27 translation groups.

**tx: 9 groups** (group sizes are wc -l on the named files)
1. Context core: ob_tx_ctx*, ob_trans_ctx*, ob_trans_ctx_lock*, ob_trans_submit_log_cb*, ob_tx_redo_submitter.h, ob_tx_ctx_mds*. 9,625 lines.
2. Service, API and ObTxDesc: ob_trans_service*, ob_tx_api*, ob_trans_define_v4*. 7,165 lines.
3. Log format and definitions: ob_tx_log*, ob_tx_big_segment_buf*, ob_trans_define*. 4,276 lines.
4. Context manager and functors: ob_trans_ctx_mgr_v4*, ob_trans_functor.h. 3,163 lines.
5. Tx data: ob_tx_data_define/op/functor*, ob_ctx_tx_data*. 3,170 lines.
6. Replay: ob_tx_replay_executor*. 874 lines.
7. ID and timestamp services, including ob_ts_mgr, the timestamp waiter and the version manager. 1,707 lines.
8. MDS notifier bridge: ob_multi_data_source*. 1,110 lines.
9. Deadlock adapter, timers, loop worker, keep-alive, ELR and the end-transaction callback. About 5.3K lines.
- About 1,100 of these lines are dead and can be dropped.

**tablelock: 4 groups**
- Object lock and map, lock memtable/table/manager, lock service with RPC structs and executor, and live detector/deadlock/callback.

**MDS: 3 groups**
- Template core (.ipp files and table/unit/row/node headers, about 9K lines), runtime utility (factory, service, list helper), and adapters, dump and merge DAG.

**logservice: 6 groups**
- palf formats (block, group and entry headers, meta, checksum): 2,771 lines.
- palf IO and storage (block manager, IO worker, storage, reader, iterators, cache, GC): 10,355 lines.
- palf core (sliding window, LSN allocator, group buffer, handle and env, state and mode managers, threads): 10,187 lines.
- Apply service: 1,631 lines.
- Replay service: 3,354 lines.
- Handler, log-service and block-manager glue: about 4.6K lines.

**standby: 2 groups**
- Log sync, gRPC and control: about 5.5K lines.
- restore/: about 9.4K lines.

**data_plane: 1 group** for this area
- Transaction, tablelock and memtable interface headers, 1,801 lines. They become the Rust trait and FFI boundary.

**Dependency constraint:** groups tx-1 through tx-6 cannot be landed without the matching parts of storage/memtable (27,023 lines) and storage/tx_table (9,956 lines). A working order is format groups first (golden-byte testable), then ID and timestamp services and palf, then the transaction core together with memtable and tx_table.
open_questions: Does seekdb promise in-place upgrade from v1.4.0 data directories (clog block_N files, ctx-table and tx-data sstable rows)? If yes, a port must match v1.4.0 byte for byte. If not, as the project's own break after v1.1.0 suggests (51cb986b9), the format can be redesigned. The repo has no upgrade or compatibility test or policy.
Are mixed-version primary/standby pairs supported? Standby ships raw palf group entries (FetchLogRes.buf), which would freeze the group-entry format as a wire format.

Was the deletion of all unittest/mittest sources in 45cbbe9e1 intentional? The commit subject is about a decimal aggregate fix. Do those tests live on in the external seekdb_test repo? That repo, and how many transaction or recovery cases it holds, could not be inspected read-only.

Are enable_early_lock_release (default True, ob_parameter_seed.ipp:555) and _enable_parallel_redo_logging (default True, :562) actually exercised in embedded and server deployments? Each adds a state (ELR_COMMIT, serial_final or parallel replay queues) that a port must reproduce or drop explicitly.
Is there a commit-latency or log-throughput baseline a port must meet? No in-repo benchmark for palf or transactions was located (not searched exhaustively).

How much of the removed-type space in ObLogBaseType (36 values, many with no registered handler) and ObTxLogType (the TX_CLEAR_LOG decode-only path) can appear in logs written by v1.4.0? Answering this needs a real v1.4.0 clog to decode, and no clog dump tool (ob_admin) is tracked in the repo.

Will the area keep shrinking? Commits such as 1cbe30f00 (2026-09-18) and the removals of XA, dup-table and multi-log-stream suggest yes. That affects whether translation should wait for the pruning to settle.

verification.structure_call_check:
I partly agree. The redesign verdict for the transaction core and for MDS is well supported:
- ObTxCtx : ObTransCtx (ObLightHashLink refcount) + ObLink holds mt_ctx_ by value (ob_tx_ctx.h:103, 598).
- It keeps busy_cbs_ as an ObDList<ObTxLogCb> (633), and each callback holds a raw ObTxCtx* (ob_trans_submit_log_cb.h:121, 155).
- The apply service reaches those callbacks through CONTAINER_OF (ob_append_callback.cpp:25).
- on_success enforces submit order with ob_abort (ob_tx_ctx.cpp:1586-1636).
- MDS is an X-macro registry expanded inside an enum body (ob_multi_data_source.h:50-68).

I disagree on four points:
1. palf's pipeline is filed under 'keep structure', yet the survey's own hard parts list its 128-bit CAS allocator (lsn_allocator.h:91-99) and the placement-new, slot-refcounted FixedSlidingWindow. Both exist to serve concurrent Paxos appends. Now that palf-lite commits on local flush (log_sliding_window.cpp:1700-1704), only palf's byte formats need to survive. The 23K-line pipeline is itself a redesign candidate, not a structure-preserving port.
2. The formats are not a clean 'derive encode/decode' job. Fields are serialized big-endian (serialization.h:212-220), but header checksums are computed over the raw in-memory C++ object image, and HEADER_SER_SIZE = sizeof(struct):
   - log_entry_header.cpp:27, 83 (xxhash_16 over this)
   - log_block_header.cpp:101-102
   - log_meta_entry_header.cpp:180-181
   - log_group_entry_header.cpp:29

   A compatible Rust port needs #[repr(C)] mirror structs with identical padding and host byte order, plus a bit-exact ob_crc64 (a CRC32C built on SSE4.2/ARM instructions, ob_crc64.cpp:344-364).
3. data_plane is the ready-made boundary only on the SQL side. 159 files outside the area include tx, tablelock or MDS headers directly: storage/tablet 27, memtable 21, observer/virtual_table 14, tx_table 12, ls 9, ddl 5, rootserver and others. 51 files outside logservice include logservice headers.
4. MDS cannot be cut out along with tx alone: mds_register.h:24-38 pulls in payload and helper types from storage/tablet, compaction and truncate_info.

The committed line is right about which files force a redesign. It is too optimistic about what can be ported as-is and about how narrow the boundary is.

missed.point: On-disk header checksums hash the in-memory C++ struct bytes, not the serialized bytes. So format compatibility depends on struct layout, padding and host byte order, and on oblib's ob_crc64, which is really CRC32C with hardware and table variants. A Rust port that 'derives encode/decode' would write logs whose checksums do not match.

verification.overall:
The survey can be trusted for sizes and for most facts at the level of individual lines. Every count reproduces exactly with an independent method: directory totals, per-extension splits, history deltas, commit counts, include sites, CI test-set size and deleted unit tests. Most cited line numbers point at the code described: the one-phase commit chain, the on_success ordering aborts, the three-latch guard, the class body split across headers, local-flush commit, the 128-bit CAS, the header version break and the standby wire path.

The errors are overstatements rather than fabrications:
- PREPARE, PRE_COMMIT and CLEAR are still read in branches that can no longer run (C5).
- The two queue concepts in replay routing are merged into one (C9).
- 'Unreferenced' dead headers are in fact still #included (C21).
- One ob_abort is misattributed to a bad refcount when it fires on a null allocator (C22).
- ob_abort is counted as 34 lines rather than 27 calls (C16).
- The MDS_ASSERT 'release builds' reasoning is wrong, although the conclusion holds.

The structure call is sound where it matters most, the transaction-context ownership cycle and the MDS metaprogramming. It is too optimistic in three places: how easily the byte formats can be kept compatible (checksums over raw struct memory), how narrow the boundary is (data_plane covers SQL only; 159 storage-side includers and a WAL shared with DDL, compaction and vector index), and whether palf's concurrent pipeline is worth keeping. Use its numbers as given and its hard-parts list as a floor, not a ceiling.

survey.what_it_is: Full-text search (five built-in tokenizers including the dictionary-driven IK Chinese tokenizer, a BM25/sparse-vector retrieval engine, and the boolean-mode query parser), vector search (HNSW/HGraph/SINDI through the vsag C++ library, a seekdb-own IVF with k-means, SIMD distance kernels, and the index lifecycle and background tasks), hybrid search (Elasticsearch-style JSON translated to SQL), and MySQL-compatible GIS (src/share/geo on boost.geometry and s2geometry, plus about 50 ST_ expressions). All four sit on top of ordinary seekdb tables; the only native libraries are vsag, s2geometry, boost.geometry and CRoaring.

survey.summary:
This area is 184,963 hand-written lines plus one 276,043-line data file. No third-party code is vendored in git: vsag, s2geometry, boost, CRoaring and ICU all arrive as prebuilt packages. Most of the code is seekdb's own logic, not thin glue.
- **FTS** calls no native library. The IK tokenizer is a port of the Java IK Analyzer and uses seekdb's charset library, not ICU.
- **IVF** is seekdb's own code, including its k-means.
- **The vsag boundary is narrow.** vsag is reached only through a roughly 2,000-line adaptor that already passes void* handles and raw arrays, plus 88 references in 8 files.
- **boost.geometry and S2 are not thin glue.** seekdb registers its own packed WKB view classes as boost.geometry types through template traits. It dispatches 22 functions across coordinate system × 7 × 7 geometry-type combinations using 716 macro-generated template specializations. It also maps boost exceptions to user-visible OB_ERR_BOOST_GEOMETRY_* errors, which the geometry tests check.
- **Three things are effectively on-disk formats and decide between keeping the library behind FFI and rewriting it:**
  - S2 cell ids are written into spatial index rows, and an update recomputes them from the old WKB.
  - The vsag snapshot serialization format is pinned to the legacy format (commit 2a27b3f11).
  - IK/ngram tokenizer output must reproduce the tokens already stored in FTS index rows.

So Rust should keep vsag and S2 behind a C shim. GIS should either stay in C++ behind a C ABI at the ST_-function level or be redesigned on georust with a high verification cost. FTS, retrieval, hybrid search, IVF and the vector distance kernels can be translated largely one-to-one.

The dictionary carries over cleanly. The main array is byte-sorted, has no duplicates and no escape sequences, so it can become a 2.78 MB newline-separated UTF-8 file loaded with include_str!. The table-based loading path is dead code and can be dropped.

The case for Rust here rests on concrete bugs:
- a data race added to parallel dictionary building and fixed 8 days later (87ab54c34, then b5d96efaf);
- a null dereference on the release path (c68c6749a);
- a leak on an error path (b5e98215e);
- a bad static_cast that crashed (a44b2526f);
- a lifetime bug in the embedding task that was fixed with a hand-written reference count ending in `delete this` (9bb15300f).

Public-surface coverage is good for GIS (42 tests, 85K lines, many ported from MySQL) and moderate for vector search (22 tests) and FTS (15 tests). It is thin for the IK tokenizer (4 tests) and zero for the hybrid-search DSL. No C++ unit tests are tracked, so every existing test survives the migration, but the IK tokenizer needs a differential corpus.

survey.structure_call:
The area splits in three.

**Translates close to one-to-one into idiomatic Rust (about 68K lines).** This covers the FTS tokenizers and dictionary code, storage/retrieval, the FTS/vector SQL and DDL glue, hybrid search, IVF/k-means and the SIMD kernels. These are shallow interface-plus-final-class hierarchies, OB_FAIL error chains that become Result and ?, arena-allocated lists that become Vec or an arena, and borrowed-pointer tokens that become &str lifetimes. The SIMD kernels map onto std::arch with #[target_feature] and runtime detection.

**Needs an ownership redesign but not an algorithm redesign.** The vector-index runtime in src/observer/vector_index and src/query/api/query/vector uses hand-written reference counts, five locks per adaptor, raw roaring64 pointers and self-deleting tasks. These become Arc plus Mutex or RwLock plus owned bitmaps.

**Cannot be translated structurally.**
- vsag and S2 stay native behind a small extern "C" shim written in C++. The shim keeps the std::streambuf bridge, the vsag Allocator, Logger and Filter subclasses, and the S2RegionCoverer call, because their outputs are persisted.
- boost.geometry is a template library instantiated over seekdb's own packed WKB view classes. It cannot be called over FFI and has no drop-in Rust equivalent. Either share/geo stays C++ behind a C ABI at the ST_-function level, or it is redesigned on georust `geo`, `proj4rs` and a hand-written WKT parser, accepting drift from MySQL-identical results and error codes.

Files that force the call: src/share/geo/ob_geo_bin_traits.h, ob_geo_tree_traits.h, ob_geo_dispatcher.h, ob_geo_bin.h, the 9 ob_geo_func_*_helper.ipp, ob_srs_wkt_parser.cpp and ob_geo_func_transform.cpp force redesign or a C++ island. src/oblib/lib/vector/ob_vsag_adaptor.cpp, src/query/api/query/vector/ob_vector_index_serialize.h and src/share/geo/ob_s2adapter.cpp / ob_geo_to_s2_visitor.cpp force a C++ FFI shim. Everything else translates one-to-one.
hard_parts: boost.geometry over seekdb types: boost traits specialized for seekdb's packed WKB view classes, which overlay raw bytes and use a const operator= hack. The boost algorithms are instantiated per (function, type1, type2). A Rust port needs a C++ island or a rewrite on georust with different numerical results. Paths: src/share/geo/ob_geo_bin_traits.h, src/share/geo/ob_geo_tree_traits.h, src/share/geo/ob_geo_bin.h.

Template and macro dispatch over coordinate system × geometry type: ObIGeoDispatcher (1,521 lines) and 716 OB_GEO_*_FUNC_BEGIN specializations split over 23 TUs, plus a 308-method virtual visitor base with 29 subclasses. In Rust this becomes enums and match, which means redesigning three parallel geometry representations: bin (20 classes), ibin (19) and tree (35). Paths: src/share/geo/ob_geo_dispatcher.h, src/share/geo/ob_geo_visitor.h, src/share/geo/ob_geo_ibin.h, src/share/geo/ob_geo_tree.h.

Exception-to-error-code mapping that users can see: the std:: and boost::geometry exception catch lists in ob_boost_geometry_exception_handle, and try/catch around std::vector growth in the S2 visitor. Rust has no equivalent, so the error codes must be reproduced by hand. Paths: src/share/geo/ob_geo_dispatcher.h:1314, src/share/geo/ob_geo_to_s2_visitor.cpp:615-647.

boost.spirit (qi/phoenix) SRS WKT grammar and boost.geometry srs transformation, a PROJ-4 port. They need replacing with nom/pest and proj4rs, or keeping in C++. Paths: src/share/geo/ob_srs_wkt_parser.cpp, src/share/geo/ob_geo_func_transform.cpp.

vsag C++ bridge: std::streambuf subclasses whose seek limits pin vsag's legacy serialization format; a vsag::Allocator subclass for memory accounting; a vsag::Logger subclass; a virtual FilterInterface callback from vsag back into seekdb that tests a roaring bitmap; and index parameters built as JSON strings with databuff_printf. Paths: src/query/api/query/vector/ob_vector_index_serialize.h, src/observer/vector_index/ob_plugin_vector_index_serialize.cpp, src/oblib/lib/vector/ob_vsag_adaptor.cpp, src/query/api/query/vector/ob_vector_index_adaptor.h:147,237.

Vector-index lifetime and locking: a hand-written reference count, an adapter guard that destructs explicitly and frees through an allocator, 2 TCRWLocks per memdata, 2 ObSpinLocks and a RWLock per adaptor, and raw roaring64 pointers shared between snapshot, delta and query paths. Mapping this onto Arc and locks without changing lock order needs the unread 4,774-line adaptor. Paths: src/query/api/query/vector/ob_vector_index_adaptor.h:416-1000, src/observer/vector_index/ob_plugin_vector_index_adaptor.cpp.

Memory accounting and recoverable OOM: CRoaring is hooked into seekdb allocators through roaring_init_memory_hook, and 41 CROARING_TRY_CATCH sites turn bad_alloc into OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED. Rust aborts on OOM by default, so keeping this behavior needs try_reserve-style APIs or allocator_api. Paths: src/share/roaringbitmap/ob_rb_memory_mgr.h, src/observer/vector_index/ob_plugin_vector_index_adaptor.cpp.

Packed variable-length cache blocks: ObFTDAT and ObArrayHashMap with char buff[1] / Entry data[1] and __attribute__((packed)), stored in and evicted from ObKVCache. They need a zero-copy byte-slice design and a Rust KV-cache binding. Paths: src/storage/fts/dict/ob_ft_dat_dict.h, src/storage/fts/dict/ob_ft_cache.h:122.

Tokenizer output is a stored contract: query tokenization, and update/delete in DOMAIN_DML_MODE_DEFAULT, re-tokenize and must reproduce the existing FTS index rows byte for byte. The IK port also depends on seekdb's charset library (ObCharset::first_valid_char, ob_mbcharlen_ptr), which must be ported or bridged first. Paths: src/sql/das/ob_das_domain_utils.cpp:940-1040, src/storage/fts/ik/ob_ik_char_util.h.

Hand-written SIMD kernels, compiled in several versions and dispatched at runtime (552 intrinsic tokens). In Rust they become unsafe std::arch code per target feature, and must be checked to keep equal floating-point accumulation order and overflow checks. Paths: src/data_plane/api/data_plane/vector/ob_vector_l2_distance.h, ob_vector_ip_distance.h, ob_vector_cosine_distance.h, ob_vector_op_common.h.

S2 types leak into core headers: ob_s2adapter.h, with S2LatLngRect in its method signatures, is included by the storage scan-parameter header and sql utils. The Rust side must hide S2 behind an opaque type before those modules move. Paths: src/data_plane/api/data_plane/access/ob_tablet_scan.h:26, src/sql/ob_sql_utils.h:25, src/sql/rewrite/ob_query_range_provider.h:23.
pain_instances: 87ab54c34 then b5d96efaf: a data race in the parallel IK dictionary build. Worker threads shared container_->fetch_info_for_dict, which does an arena allocation and an ObList push_back with no lock, until per-thread handles were pre-allocated 8 days later. Rust's Send/Sync would have rejected sharing &mut container across threads. Paths: src/storage/fts/dict/ob_ft_range_dict.cpp, src/storage/fts/dict/ob_ft_cache_container.h:55-68.

survey.public_surface_tests:
All tracked tests for this area run through SQL (mysqltest or obtest). No tracked test uses C++ internals: unittest/ holds only .gitignore files, and deps/oblib/unittest has 2 jemalloc tests. So every test survives a translation unchanged.
- tools/deploy/mysql_test/test_suite/geometry: 42 .test and 42 .result files, 85,270 lines together. 39 of them call ST_ functions. Examples: vector_index_basic, vector_index_ivfflat_{basic,dml,scan,post_create}, sparse_vector_index_vsag_{ddl,query}, create_table_with_hybrid_vector_index, vector_similarity, vector_calc_{gbk,utf8}_mysql, rebuild_vector_index, all_virtual_vector_index_info.

Only 4 tests use the ik parser (cn_word.test has 9 uses) and tokenize() appears in 3 tests, so the 275,908-word IK dictionary is exercised by a handful of sentences.

survey.units_of_work:
Natural units are directory-sized crates or modules. There are 14:
1. IK dictionary data: 1 file becomes 3 UTF-8 resources. The main list is 275,908 sorted, unique lines (2.78 MB), loaded with include_str!, or the trie can be pre-built in build.rs. This is mechanical and done by a script.
2. FTS tokenizer library, src/storage/fts minus the data file: 71 files, 10,526 lines, in 4 groups:
   - the 5 parsers with their descriptors;
   - ik/ processors, token chain and arbitrator (13 files);
   - dict/ trie, cache and hub (27 files, of which roughly 800 lines of table-loading code are dead);
   - utils/ ngram and unicode (5 files).
   It depends on a Rust charset module and a KV-cache binding.
3. FTS boolean-mode query parser: 6 tracked files (ftsparser.y, ftsblex.l, fts_base.c/h, fts_parse.c/h), a rewrite with a hand-written parser or a parser generator.
4. Sparse retrieval engine: storage/retrieval, data_plane/retrieval and das/iter/sparse_retrieval, 41 files and 13,022 lines. The iterator interfaces become traits.
5. FTS SQL/DDL glue: resolver, rootserver tasks, tokenize/bm25/doc_id expressions and das text_retrieval iterators, 28 files and 11,981 lines. It moves with the SQL and DDL units.
6. vsag shim: src/oblib/lib/vector, 4 files and 1,991 lines. It stays C++ and becomes the extern "C" boundary. The streambuf and allocator bridges from ob_vector_index_serialize.h and ObVsagSearchAlloc move into it.
7. Vector-index runtime: src/observer/vector_index (33 files, 25,210 lines) plus query/api/query/vector and query/vector (9 files, 5,126 lines). It needs the ownership redesign.
8. Distance kernels: data_plane/vector and storage/vector_type, 44 files and 5,444 lines.
9. IVF: storage/vector_index k-means (2 files, 1,951 lines), plus ob_das_ivf_scan_iter and the ivf expressions inside unit 10.
10. Vector SQL/DDL glue: 89 files and 33,407 lines, including the hnsw/ivf/spiv DAS iterators (about 9.6K lines), 42 expression files, ob_vec_index_builder_util (5.6K lines) and the rootserver vec tasks.
11. Hybrid search: 10 files and 6,060 lines, self-contained, translating JSON to SQL.
12. GIS core, src/share/geo: 179 files and 47,033 hand-written lines, plus 651 generated lines to regenerate with prost. It is either one C++ island behind a C ABI, or on a rewrite about 7 groups: representations, 22 function types, visitors, SRS/WKT, S2 adapter, MVT, and utils/cast.
13. GIS expressions: 104 files and 14,674 lines, about 50 ST_ expressions (48 ST_ .cpp files).
14. Shared domain-index DAS code: 6 files and 4,211 lines.
The roaring glue (2 files, 293 lines) goes with unit 7.
open_questions: Must seekdb data written before the migration stay readable afterwards: vsag snapshots, S2 cell ids in spatial indexes, and FTS token rows? This one requirement decides whether vsag and S2 must be kept behind FFI and whether tokenizers must match token for token.
Does any pure-Rust S2 port reproduce C++ S2RegionCoverer coverings bit for bit with max_cells=4, max_level=30, level_mod=1? This cannot be tested read-only.
How many of the 42 geometry tests would pass on georust geo/proj4rs instead of boost.geometry? It needs a run. The expected results come from boost behavior, some of it ported from MySQL.

Does FTS update/delete in practice take the re-tokenize path (DOMAIN_DML_MODE_DEFAULT) or the FTS_DOC_WORD scan path (DOMAIN_DML_MODE_FT_SCAN)? With the first, a tokenizer difference would leave index rows that are never deleted; with the second, only query results change. When each mode is chosen was not traced.

How far do s2geometry and boost headers reach through ob_sql_utils.h and ob_tablet_scan.h by transitive includes, and what does that cost in compile time? A compile database is needed, and build_release/ was off-limits.
Do the hybrid_search mysqltest cases named in psmalltest.py exist outside this repository? If not, hybrid search has no regression coverage today.

Can seekdb's per-module memory accounting and recoverable OOM (vsag allocator, roaring memory hook, CROARING_TRY_CATCH) be reproduced with a Rust global allocator, or do they need nightly allocator_api?
Is vsag's HNSW/HGraph build deterministic enough for vector_index .result files to stay stable if the calling code changes thread counts or batch sizes?
Did 87ab54c34's parallel trie build change the order of handles, and does the range-id to cache-key mapping depend on it? The race fix was read, but the ordering was not checked.

The optimizer has about 944 vector-index tokens and 280 FTS tokens, ob_tsc_cg_service.cpp has 362 matching lines, and storage/ddl/ob_ddl_pipeline.cpp has 180. verification.structure_call_check: I partly agree. Keeping vsag behind a small C++ shim is right. The C++-only bridges are real: std::streambuf subclasses in ob_vector_index_serialize.h:32-109, vsag::Allocator/Logger/FilterInterface subclasses in ob_vector_index_adaptor.h:147,237 and ob_vector_util.h:35. The snapshot format is pinned (2a27b3f11). Keeping S2 native is also right, and easier than the survey suggests: all SQL-side use goes through seekdb's own ObS2Adapter (ob_range_generator.cpp:1617-1642, ob_table_scan_op.cpp:3511, ob_das_domain_utils.cpp:166), which is already a narrow wrapper. Calling boost.geometry the hardest part is right (ob_geo_bin_traits.h, ob_geo_bin.h pack(1) views, 710 dispatcher specializations). I disagree on two points. (1) The 'C ABI at the ST_-function level' boundary for GIS is too narrow. share/geo is also called from casts (ob_datum_cast.cpp has 103 geo references; share/object/ob_obj_cast.cpp), the range generator (sql/rewrite, 5 files), the SRS service (observer/omt/ob_srs_service.cpp), dml_service, the aggregate processor and table_scan_op. ObSpatialMBR is an OB_UNIS-serialized type in the scan params (ob_s2adapter.h:60, ob_tablet_scan.h:346). boost.geometry reaches 25 expression files through ob_geo_func_register.h -> ob_geo_dispatcher.h -> ob_geo_func_common.h:30. A C++ GIS island therefore needs cast, range and SRS entry points as well, not only ST_ functions. (2) The 'translates close to one-to-one' group is not a unit that can move on its own. Its vector and FTS SQL glue depends on plan code in src/sql/optimizer (ob_log_table_scan.cpp, ob_join_order.cpp, ob_log_plan.cpp), in src/sql/code_generator/ob_tsc_cg_service.cpp, and in the DDL pipeline (storage/ddl/ob_ddl_pipeline.cpp, ob_vector_index_ddl_pipeline.h). The translation is easy line by line, but the order is decided by when the optimizer, DAS and DDL move. The three-way split itself (easy translation, ownership redesign for the vector-index runtime, keep native for vsag/S2/boost.geometry) is a sound way to divide the area.

missed.point: Vector and FTS query planning and DDL live in core SQL and storage code, not in the counted 'glue'. A Rust vector or FTS module cannot move without the optimizer, the code generator and the DDL pipeline, or without a boundary cut through them.

verification.overall: The survey can be trusted for facts and counts, less for its size framing and boundaries. Every cited path, commit and line range I opened was accurate. The core counts come out the same with a different method: the dictionary entries, uniqueness and byte size, the FTS, vector, geo and hybrid line counts, the roaring calls, the boost token counts and the SIMD token count. The behavior claims describe what the code really does: the vsag stream bridge and legacy format pin, S2 cell ids in spatial index rows, the boost exception mapping, the race and its fix, the explicit destructor call in reset(), and the STRLEN before the null check. The errors I found are small: 710 not 716 dispatcher specializations, 177 not 179 hand-written geo files, the package is DBMS_HYBRID_SEARCH, vsag is 0.18.0 on Android, protobuf-c is missing, and the beng parser copies its tokens. The weaker parts are framing. The '68K one-to-one' figure does not match the survey's own buckets. The area boundary leaves out the large amount of vector and FTS logic in the optimizer, code generator and DDL pipeline. The GIS C-ABI boundary is drawn too narrowly. And the survey treats tokenizer drift as a stored-data risk for deletes, when the code actually reads old tokens back from the doc-word table. Its main recommendations still stand: keep vsag and S2 behind a C++ shim, treat boost.geometry as the hardest piece, and translate FTS, IVF and hybrid search directly. But any plan built on it should add the optimizer/DDL coupling and the wider GIS entry points before sizing or ordering the work.

survey.area: oblib (src/oblib: lib/, common/, rpc/, easy/, grpc/)
survey.what_it_is: src/oblib is seekdb's base library. lib/ holds the runtime substrate: allocators, containers, hash maps, strings, locks, threads, timers, logging, serialization, macros, charset, compression and checksums. common/ holds the value model that sits on top of lib/: ObObj, ObDatum, rows and rowkeys, ObNumber decimal, wide integers, datetime and timezone conversion, JSON, XML and collection types. Next to these sit the C++ glue for the Rust sql-nio MySQL front end (rpc/), leftover libeasy headers (easy/), and a standby gRPC service (grpc/).

survey.summary:
oblib sits at the bottom of every other module, and its hand-written core is only about two-thirds of its size: 254K of the 382K lines. The rest is data, generated code, vendored code, or code ported from MySQL, and about 85K lines (22%) are unreferenced. That unreferenced part includes the whole 32K-line lib/codec, with its generated SIMD bit-packing, and the 39K lines of built-in timezone tables that nothing reads.

The layering is clean at the top level: lib/ never includes common/ (0 files). Inside each layer, though, directories include each other: there are 44 such directory pairs, for example alloc<->allocator and oblog<->utility. So a Rust port cannot map directories to crates one-to-one; the substrate would need to become one crate or be re-cut.

The types everyone depends on are the ones that force design work before any translation:
- `int ret`/OB_FAIL error codes appear in 3,160 of 5,796 non-oblib files.
- ObIAllocator, a virtual allocator passed by reference, appears in 2,358 files. Allocation failure is an expected, handled error: 6,302 `OB_FAIL(x.push_back(` lines. Rust's std containers abort on out-of-memory instead.
- ObString, ObObj and ObDatum are non-owning raw-pointer views into arena memory. ObObj is a 16-byte union, ObDatum a packed union of 20 typed pointers, and ObString uses const_cast so one type serves as both read-only view and writable buffer. In Rust these become lifetime-bound borrows or unsafe views, and that choice spreads into sql and storage.
- The macro frameworks (OB_UNIS serialization, TO_STRING_KV/K(), LST_DO_CODE, ObObj compare tables) map naturally to Rust derive macros. But the OB_UNIS byte format (vi64 version, 5-byte fixed length slot, strict version match) and the formats of ObNumber, JSON binary and CRC32C have to be reproduced byte for byte if old data must stay readable.

Much of lib/ has direct Rust equivalents: containers, hashing, compression, CRC32C, base64, locks, stack switching (stacker), backtraces, and gRPC (tonic from a 135-line .proto). Value semantics that must match MySQL have no crate and are pure functions best translated one-to-one: ObNumber, datetime parsing, utf8mb4_general_ci, JSON path and binary format, ObObj compare/cast. seekdb already builds only 3 collations, so the charset port is small.

oblib reaches upward through 17 weak-symbol definitions and ambient thread-locals (Worker::self_, CURRENT_CONTEXT). A Rust port needs explicit registration for these.

Verification is expensive here. Only 2 C++ unit tests remain, both allocator tests that use internals. The public mysqltest surface touches oblib-backed features thinly: decimal 43 .test files, collation 30, JSON 17, timezone 3, XML 0.

Real memory-safety bugs in this area in 2026 are ones Rust's ownership rules would have removed: a worker use-after-free and then a double-free in the thread pool's intrusive list, UB from memcpy on NULL, and hash-bucket locks left unconstructed because the code relied on zeroed memory.

survey.structure_call:
oblib splits into two halves that need different treatment.

The substrate cannot be translated one-to-one into idiomatic Rust and has to be redesigned: allocators, containers, hash maps, strings, locks, threads, logging, serialization and the macro layer. Reasons:
- Errors are `int ret` codes and allocation failure is a normal error. Rust needs Result plus try_reserve-style containers.
- ObIAllocator is a virtual allocator passed by reference, and there is an ambient CURRENT_CONTEXT arena. Rust needs arena lifetimes, or allocator-aware types with explicit handles.
- ObString, ObObj and ObDatum are non-owning raw-pointer views into arena memory. They must become lifetime-bound borrows or deliberately unsafe views, and that choice spreads to every sql and storage signature.
- Behavior is generated by macros and SFINAE: OB_UNIS, TO_STRING_KV, copy_assign/construct_assign, ObObj function tables. Rust needs derive macros and traits.
- 17 weak symbols, the intrusive lists, and assembly stack switching need Rust-native replacements: registration, owned collections, stacker.
- Directories include each other in 44 pairs, so the directory tree cannot become crates as it is.

The value model and the data-format code can be translated one-to-one, function by function: ObNumber, wide integers, datetime/timezone conversion, utf8mb4_general_ci, JSON path and binary, XML/XPath, ObObj compare/cast, and the OB_UNIS byte codec. They are mostly pure code over bytes that must match MySQL and the on-disk layout exactly.

Vendored, generated and dead code should be replaced or dropped, not translated: zstd, xxhash and gRPC by crates; codec and the timezone tables by deletion.

Files that force the call: src/oblib/lib/alloc/ob_iallocator.h, lib/allocator/page_arena.h, lib/rc/context.h, lib/container/ob_array.h, lib/container/ob_raw_se_array.h, lib/string/ob_string.h, common/object/ob_object.h, common/datum/ob_datum.h, lib/utility/ob_unify_serialize.h, lib/utility/ob_macro_utils.h, lib/utility/ob_print_utils.h, lib/alloc/alloc_struct.h.
hard_parts: Arena lifetimes for non-owning views: ObString (lib/string/ob_string.h:203-211, const_cast in assign_ptr), ObObjValue raw pointers (common/object/ob_object.h:1257-1285), ObDatum packed union of typed pointers (common/datum/ob_datum.h:106-131). A lifetime parameter or an unsafe-view decision here reaches the roughly 1,000-1,600 files that use these types.

ObIAllocator as a virtual interface passed as `ObIAllocator &` in 2,358 files, plus ObMemAttr labels and 8 ctx ids for memory accounting (lib/alloc/ob_iallocator.h, lib/alloc/alloc_struct.h:113-139, lib/utility/ob_mod_define.h:18-26). Rust's Allocator trait is unstable, so this needs allocator_api2/bumpalo or a custom handle type.

Fallible allocation as a normal error (6,302 `OB_FAIL(x.push_back(` lines) and fallible copy via `int assign(const T&)` picked at compile time by SFINAE (common/meta_programming/ob_meta_copy.h, lib/utility/utility.h:1128-1210, lib/container/ob_array.h:102-255). Rust std Vec/HashMap abort on out-of-memory.

The custom allocator's internals: AChunk/ABlock/AObject headers with magic codes and free-list pointers stored in the same union as user data (lib/alloc/alloc_struct.h:162-282), mmap-aligned 2MB chunks (lib/resource/achunk_mgr.cpp), a libc malloc override (lib/alloc/malloc_hook.cpp), and jemalloc memory-sanity redzones (lib/allocator/ob_jemalloc_sanity.cpp, ob_sanity_libc_wrap.cpp). All of this is unsafe Rust, or has to be replaced by a #[global_allocator] plus arenas.

Preprocessor frameworks with no direct Rust counterpart that must become proc-macros: variadic argument counting and APPLY chains (lib/utility/ob_macro_utils.h, 427 defines), OB_UNIS (lib/utility/ob_unify_serialize.h), TO_STRING_KV/K() (lib/utility/ob_print_utils.h:1038, lib/oblog/ob_log_module.h:1240), per-type DEF_*_FUNCS (common/object/ob_obj_funcs.h), the compare-function matrix (common/object/ob_obj_compare.cpp, 177 defines), and the X-macro tables LATCH_DEF (204 rows, lib/stat/ob_latch_define.h), WAIT_EVENT_DEF (89, lib/wait_event/ob_wait_event.h) and STAT_EVENT (358, lib/statistic_event/ob_stat_event.h).

Byte-exact formats if old data must stay readable: the OB_UNIS envelope and LEB128 vi64 (lib/utility/serialization.h:96,308-340), ObNumber base-1e9 digits and Desc (common/number/ob_number_v2.h:143), OceanBase JSON binary (common/json_type/ob_json_bin.cpp, 4,721 lines), CRC32C under the name crc64 (lib/checksum/ob_crc64.cpp:357-372), and frames written by zstd 1.3.8.

Upward calls through 17 weak symbols (e.g. lib/oblog/ob_log.cpp:73, common/mysqlclient/ob_mysql_proxy.cpp:29, lib/worker.cpp:33,39). Rust has no link-time override, so these need callback registration or traits injected at startup.

Implicit per-thread state: Worker::self_ `static __thread` (lib/worker.h), the CURRENT_CONTEXT memory-context stack (lib/rc/context.h:46-67), and RLOCAL thread_locals (lib/coro/co_var.h; 135 lines in 69 files).

Lock-free structures with custom memory reclamation: ObQSync / RetireStation / hazard refs (lib/allocator/ob_qsync.h, ob_retire_station.h, ob_hazard_ref.h), ObLinkHashMap (lib/hash/ob_link_hashmap.h), ObLinearHashMap (lib/hash/ob_linear_hash_map.h, 2,507 lines). Rust would need crossbeam-epoch or haphazard, with different semantics.

Futex-based latches that feed latch-id and wait-event statistics, with per-OS emulation (lib/lock/ob_latch.cpp, lib/lock/ob_futex.cpp, lib/lock/ob_futex.h). parking_lot does not record latch ids or wait-event stats.

Intrusive lists holding raw pointers to objects owned elsewhere: ObDList/ObDLinkBase (lib/list/ob_dlist.h; 63 and 61 files outside oblib), the worker list in lib/thread/ob_simple_thread_pool.h:59,123, and the AChunk prev_/next_ lists (lib/alloc/alloc_struct.h:178-179).

Stack switching in inline assembly per ABI (lib/utility/ob_smart_call.cpp) and SMART_VAR/HEAP_VAR (lib/utility/ob_smart_var.h; 150 and 78 files). stacker covers the stack switching, but the stack budget constants (ob_smart_call.h ALL_STACK_LIMIT etc.) need re-tuning.
SIMD intrinsics in live code: lib/container/ob_bitmap.cpp (37 lines), with an x86-to-NEON shim at lib/codec/ob_sse_to_neon.h. The large generated SIMD block is dead.

Unresolved C++ third-party dependencies with C++ APIs: VSAG vector index (lib/vector/ob_vsag_adaptor.cpp uses std::shared_ptr<vsag::Index>, tl::expected and a virtual FilterInterface) needs a C shim. libxml2 SAX (common/xml/ob_libxml2_sax_handler.cpp) and rapidjson (common/json_type/ob_json_parse.cpp) would be swapped for Rust parsers, with a risk of semantic drift in XPath/JSON path behavior.
pain_instances: 40fcfa901 (2026-05-18) "fix worker use-after-free and add missing lock in th_worker", then 328253969 (2026-05-26) "fix: worker double-free". Both are in lib/thread/ob_simple_thread_pool.ipp. The Worker lived in the intrusive ObDList workers_ and was freed with manual OB_DELETE on several paths. reap_workers() could delete a worker whose start() was still running, and the first fix caused a double free. The current code adds the worker to the list only after start() succeeds (ob_simple_thread_pool.ipp:158-163). With owned JoinHandle/Arc, safe Rust would not compile the use-after-free or the double free.

1e4f589b8 (2026-04-20): MEMCPY/MEMMOVE/MEMCMP with NULL pointers and n==0 is UB; Linux glibc tolerated it and the Windows CRT aborted. The fix wraps them in ob_memcpy_safe etc. (still at lib/utility/alloc_assist.h:52-71). The same commit zero-fills uninitialized discrete-vector ptr/len arrays that only happened to be zero on Linux. Rust slices cannot be NULL, and reading uninitialized memory requires explicit MaybeUninit.

89a52de4c (2026-04-09) "fix some core on windows": (a) hash bucket arrays skipped constructors on Linux, relying on memset(0) being a valid pthread lock; macOS and Windows need placement new (still at lib/hash/ob_hashutils.h:1223-1230; same pattern in ob_hashtable.h ObHashTableBucket). (b) Windows futex_wake returned 0, which made ObLatchWaitQueue::wake_up wake every waiter (lib/lock/ob_futex.h). (c) The assembly stack switch crashed on Win64 until an ABI-specific jump_call and TIB patching were added (lib/utility/ob_smart_call.cpp, ob_smart_call.h). (a) is removed by Rust's rule that values must be initialized; (c) is replaced by the stacker/psm crates.

6bd81a07b (2026-02-03) "fix rpc mempool use-after-free issue" in deps/oblib/src/rpc/obrpc/ob_local_procedure_call.h. That file has since been deleted with obrpc, so this is historical evidence for this code family only.

Defensive code that exists only to catch memory errors: magic codes in every allocation header and at the tail (lib/alloc/alloc_struct.h:243-282; 147 MAGIC lines in 42 oblib files; 211 abort_unless lines in 35 files, e.g. ObAllocAlign::free_align in lib/alloc/ob_iallocator.h); a 16-frame backtrace per allocation plus unfreed-object scans for leak finding (alloc_struct.h:293, lib/alloc/object_set.cpp:461); a 910-line memory-sanity redzone system (lib/allocator/ob_memory_sanity.h, ob_jemalloc_sanity.cpp, ob_sanity_libc_wrap.cpp); and a disabled mprotect guard for stray writes into hash buckets (lib/hash/mprotect.h, `#if 0`).

Const-correctness hole: ObString::assign_ptr const_casts const char* to char* (lib/string/ob_string.h:205), so writing through a read-only borrowed view is not a compile error. Rust separates &[u8] from &mut [u8].
survey.public_surface_tests:
oblib has no public surface of its own. It is exercised only indirectly through SQL, by tools/deploy/mysql_test (283 .test files) and tools/obtest (510 .test files).

Counts of mysql_test .test files that touch oblib-backed features (git grep -l -i over 'tools/deploy/mysql_test/*.test'; the obtest count follows in brackets):
- decimal/numeric (ObNumber, wide_integer, ObObj compare/cast): 43 [3], e.g. test_suite/datatype/t/div.test, minus.test
- collate/collation/character set (the 3 live collations): 30 [10], e.g. test_suite/expr/t/collation_expr.test, t/add.test
- json (json_type): 17 [2], of which 6 call json_* functions, e.g. test_suite/fts_index/t/basic_dml.test, test_suite/geometry/t/geometry_bugfix_mysql.test. There is no dedicated JSON suite.
- time_zone/convert_tz (timezone): 3 [2], e.g. test_suite/type_date/t/daylight_saving_time.test. The type_date suite as a whole has 10 .test files touching ob_time_convert.
- compress/zstd/lz4: 12 [21]
- cast/convert: 26 [3]
- XML functions (extractvalue/updatexml): 0, although 15K lines of common/xml back ob_expr_extract_value and ob_expr_update_xml.
- Collection/array types (common/udt): the array suite, 2 .test.
- vector_index: 22 .test files, which reach the VSAG adaptor in lib/vector.

Tests that use internals: only deps/oblib/unittest/lib/alloc/test_jemalloc_hook.cpp and deps/oblib/unittest/lib/allocator/test_malloc_backend.cpp, and both would be rewritten. No tests remain for containers, hash maps, serialization, ObNumber, charset or JSON. Equivalence for the byte formats (OB_UNIS, ObNumber, JSON binary, CRC32C) would need new golden or differential tests generated from the C++ build.
survey.units_of_work:
Excluding vendored and generated code, oblib has 500 translation units (a header plus its .cpp/.ipp counted as one) in 77 directories. By size: 25 units of 2,000 lines or more, 104 of 500-1,999, 278 of 100-499, and 93 under 100 (awk over git ls-files, stem = path without extension).

Suggested grouping:
(1) Substrate, redesigned directory by directory (about 40 lib/ directories, roughly 140K lines): alloc, allocator, resource, rc, container, hash, list, queue, objectpool, string, lock, thread, task, oblog, utility, stat, wait_event, statistic_event, trace, time, signal, file, guard, atomic, and so on. The 44 directory pairs that include each other mean these land as one or a few crates, not one crate per directory. The first units, needed by everything else, are the error type, the allocator/arena handle, fallible containers, strings, the OB_UNIS codec derive, and the logging/printing derive.
(2) Value model, translated one-to-one per header/source pair (about 20 common/ directories plus lib/charset, roughly 110K lines live): object, datum, row, rowkey, number, wide_integer, timezone (minus the dead tables), json_type, xml, udt, lob, enumset, sql_mode, mysqlclient.
(3) Replaced, not translated: zstd, zlib and xxhash by crates; grpc by tonic/prost from standbyservice.proto (1 unit); rpc/obmysql + frame (61 files, 6,176 lines) merged into the existing rust/sql-nio boundary.
(4) Deleted: lib/codec (32,109 lines), the timezone tables (38,963 lines), 7 unbuilt sources, 21 never-included headers.
open_questions: Does a Rust seekdb have to read data files and redo logs written by the C++ build? This decides whether the OB_UNIS, ObObj/ObNumber serialization, JSON binary, CRC32C and zstd-1.3.8 formats must be byte-exact, or can be redesigned behind a one-time migration.

Must memory limits keep surfacing OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED to the SQL client (fallible allocation everywhere), or is abort-on-out-of-memory acceptable? And must the per-label/per-ctx memory accounting (ObMemAttr labels, 8 ctx ids) be kept? This decides custom allocator handles versus a global jemalloc plus arenas.
Is the standby gRPC service (grpc/, built only with OB_ENABLE_STANDBY) in scope for the migration?

Was ob_ctype_uca.cc dropped on purpose, given only 3 collations are valid? Where did uca900_data.h go (it is untracked, and a filesystem search outside build_release found nothing)? Can the 244-entry ObCollationType enum shrink?

I could not confirm read-only that lib/codec, the timezone tables and the 21 never-included headers are also absent from the linked binary (e.g. through symbols kept alive by LTO or dlsym). That needs a build or nm check, which the no-build rule forbids.
Which oblib code paths does mysqltest actually cover at runtime? That needs a coverage build. The grep counts above only show which features are mentioned.
Do Rust crates (hashbrown/dashmap, parking_lot, crossbeam-epoch) match ObHashMap, ObLinearHashMap, ObLatch and QSync throughput under seekdb's thread counts? That needs benchmarks.

How many OB_DEF_SERIALIZE hand-written bodies and legacy NEED_SERIALIZE_AND_DESERIALIZE types (196 and 86 lines across src) hide conditional or union encodings that a derive macro cannot express? Each would have to be catalogued.
Can the VSAG C++ dependency stay in C++ behind a C shim, given the adaptor already exposes mostly void*-handle functions (lib/vector/ob_vsag_adaptor.h), or is a Rust vector index planned?
