verification.structure_call_check:
I partly agree. These parts hold: point the generators at Rust output (gen_errno.pl, gen_ob_sys_variables.py, generate_inner_table_schema.py), treat the bison grammars separately (sql_parser_mysql_mode.y: 758 rules, 197 opt_*, 18,723 lines), split the 54 oversize hand-written files, convert data by script, and replace vendored C with crates.
I disagree with four points.
(1) 'Header cycles (69 files) set the minimum crate boundaries' is wrong. The cycles that matter for crates are between directories, not between headers:
- At directory level, one include cycle joins 110 directories and 4,108 live files across sql, storage, rootserver and pl.
- At the level of the survey's own 52 groups, 42 groups form a single cycle and the 10 oblib groups form another. Part of that is caused by the grouping: share-schema contains observer/schema, search-vector-retrieval spans observer + storage + share + sql, jobs-scheduler spans observer + rootserver, and ai-functions spans share + observer + sql.
- At top-level module level the layering is almost clean. Only 4 include edges tie sql and storage together: storage/ddl/ob_tablet_slice_writer.cpp -> sql/engine/ob_batch_rows.h, 2 edges from sql/engine/px/ob_px_sub_coord.cpp to storage/ddl, and storage/ddl/ob_ddl_insert_dag.cpp -> rootserver/ddl_task/ob_ddl_task.h. Cutting those leaves cycles of 57 sql directories (2,408 files), 38 storage directories (1,367), 38 oblib directories (447) and 20 share directories (608).
(2) 'Each stem maps to one Rust module' ignores that 118 forwarding headers plus query/api and data_plane/api keep declarations in one group and the implementing .cpp in another. Examples: query/api/query/engine/expr/ob_expr_in.h is implemented in sql/engine/expr/ob_expr_in.cpp; sql/pl/ob_pl.h is implemented in src/pl/ob_pl.cpp. Rust requires a struct's inherent impl to be in the crate that defines the struct.
(3) 'Class hierarchies kept as they are' needs one design decision made before any stem is translated, because Rust has no inheritance. The tree has 4,364 derived class declarations, 17,225 lines containing `virtual` and 16,392 #define lines.
(4) Hard part (e), 'generated SIMD code maps to std::arch', should be a check for deletion first: the codec library has no users outside its own directory.

verification.overall:
You can trust the survey's measurements; its readings of what they mean need rework. With an independent method I reproduced:
- the file set, line and byte totals
- all five category totals
- the dead set (exactly, apart from one .def labelled data)
- all 52 hand-written group rows of the TSV
- the one-level context distribution (within about 1%)
- the 30-stem sample, to the token
- the header-cycle, forwarder and fan-in counts
- the test-coverage greps.
The factual errors are small: the 50 build-time files are not all inner-table files, 358 not 359 cast functions, the cap-based unit counts are a little high, the largest header cycle has 8 files not 9, a sixth generator was missed, ob_keybtree.cpp is live, and 'almost every oversize file is one class' is too strong (ob_schema_struct.h has 93 classes, ob_raw_expr.h about 48, ob_rpc_struct.h 149 structs).
The weaker parts are the interpretations. The 2.4M-token 'typical' closure comes from a biased sample; over all stems the median is 1.43M. The claim that header cycles set crate boundaries is wrong: cycles between directories and between groups are far larger, and the survey's own grouping across modules makes them worse. The stem-as-unit model ignores declaration/implementation pairs split across groups. Include-only dead detection misses compiled code that nothing calls, such as the codec library.
Use the ledger's counts and token sizes as they are. Rebuild the grouping, crate plan and dead-code estimate before they feed the cost formula.

survey.summary: The large feature-removal wave ran from 2026-06-11 to 2026-08-25 and is now over. C/C++ source fell from 6.62M lines (2026-06-23) to 2.84M (2026-08-22), then only another 2.4% to 2.77M by HEAD. In the last 30 days the ordinary edit rate in src/ C/C++ is 32 deduplicated commits, +3,895/-3,944 lines, about 0.3% of the tree per month. Three bulk commits removed another 80,040 lines (8a8d6f5a8 log reduction -59,109 on 2026-09-16, d51422b54 DirectLoadMgr, e2dc7eecf drift fix). Cutting is still going on at a lower rate. Open PR #1356 removes obmalloc (-12,094 lines in 227 files), and #1427 rewrites OB_FAIL branches to ASSERT_COND in 130 files. 18 open issues titled "Remove ..." act as the removal backlog, since docs/, AGENTS.md and README* state no roadmap. Raw git numbers overstate churn. Until 2026-08-25 the same change often landed twice, once through the obdev mirror and once as a GitHub PR, and then got reconciled by 38 "fix drift between internal and public master" commits (131 of 869 commits are exact patch duplicates). Large deletions also rode inside commits with unrelated messages (45cbbe9e1, 706253423). obdev is a mirror of seekdb's own internal repo, oceanbase-lite on gitlab.oceanbase-dev.com, not of OceanBase mainline. 25/25 sampled commits have no body beyond seekdb-engineer Co-authored-by trailers, and none has a mainline marker. The mirror stopped on 2026-08-25: all 57 commits on live master since then are GitHub PRs or direct pushes, and internal MRs now arrive as PRs (#1340, #1341). Fixes from OceanBase mainline did flow in, as 103 [CP] commits since 2025-09. That flow peaked at 58 in 2025-12 and has been almost zero since May 2026 (one in June, from 4_6_0_release). Upstream sharing is still high: 22 of 30 sampled hand-written files are near-identical (at least 90% of lines matched) to OB CE master, 90.1% line-weighted, and 75.6% of src C/C++ files exist at the same path in OB CE master, which keeps fixing them (29 commits to the 30 sampled files since 2026-03-28). So a rewrite gives up a fix stream seekdb has mostly stopped using, but one it could still use. Parallel lines a port would also have to absorb: 34 live branches were active in the last 30 days, the largest being feature/plugin (+105,879 code lines), namespace-worker-proxy-v20 (+17,592), feat/embedded-mode (+16,487), feature/webassembly-shell (+11,081), plus the release/1.4.0 maintenance branch. Judgment: the tree is settling but is still being cut.

survey.structure_call: This area does not decide translation style on its own, but it pushes toward a structure-preserving, file-for-file translation for as long as the C++ tree keeps changing. 75.6% of src C/C++ files still sit at the same path in OceanBase CE master, and about 90% of sampled lines match. A port that keeps the file and function layout can therefore keep replaying both seekdb's own fixes (about 8K lines a month, concentrated in sql/optimizer and sql/rewrite) and any OB mainline fix onto the Rust side. A redesign breaks both links for good. Against that, the mainline stream seekdb actually uses has nearly dried up (1 [CP] commit since May 2026, none since 2026-08-25), so giving it up costs little today but closes an option. A port should also start only after the in-flight structural PRs land (#1356 obmalloc removal, #1427 OB_FAIL to ASSERT_COND, #1351 plugin system), because they change the idioms a translator's rules would depend on. Files that force the call: src/sql/engine/ob_physical_plan.cpp, src/sql/engine/table/ob_table_scan_op.h and src/sql/engine/join/ob_join_filter_op.cpp (the shared files OB master changes most), plus the seekdb high-churn directories src/sql/optimizer, src/sql/rewrite, src/sql/resolver and src/storage/tx.
hard_parts: Keeping up with SQL correctness fixes during a port: in the last 30 days 11 of 16 ordinary src/sql commits hit src/sql/optimizer and src/sql/rewrite (SQLancer-found regressions, e.g. b228105f0, 192aedaf6, 402f0e25b). Each has to be replayed on the Rust side, or those directories frozen.

The allocator under the code is being replaced: open PR #1356 (codex/remove-obmalloc-upstream, 227 files, -12,094 lines) removes obmalloc for jemalloc, which touches src/oblib/lib/alloc and every ob_malloc caller (186 files at HEAD). A port started before it lands would be porting an allocator on its way out.
The error-handling idiom is changing: PR #1427 (feature/assert, 130 files) rewrites infallible OB_FAIL branches to ASSERT_COND, and a translator's rules would key on exactly the OB_FAIL/ret pattern.

Parallel lines that would need re-porting or merging first: feature/plugin (include/seekdb/plugin, plugins/gis, +105,879 code lines), feat/embedded-mode (C ABI, 197 commits ahead), feature/webassembly-shell (260 code files), codex/namespace-worker-proxy-v20 (src/observer/namespace_worker_*.ipp, 223 commits ahead), feature/rust (#1412, a second Rust effort by another author).

A released version is maintained in parallel: release/1.4.0 (6 ahead, 692 behind master) receives cherry-picked fixes (#1389 '[1.4.0] Fix block stat memtable refresh rowkey boundary'). The C++ code base has to stay alive for released versions during any port.

History can't be trusted as a change feed. The same change landed twice on the internal-mirror and GitHub lines (131 exact duplicate patches since 2026-03-28), drift-fix commits reconciled the two, and large deletions rode in commits with unrelated messages (45cbbe9e1, 706253423). A sync tool for a port must diff trees, not follow commit messages.

Upstream divergence differs by module: src/share matches OB CE paths for only 52% of files and src/oblib for 70%, versus 90% for src/sql. The option to keep taking OB mainline fixes is worth the most for sql/ and storage/, and the least for share/ and the seekdb-only modules (src/query, src/data_plane, src/standby).
pain_instances: 6da784ac1 (twin e66776e2d, #1319): wrong buffer length passed to databuff_printf (buf_len instead of extra_print_buf_size) in src/observer/virtual_table/ob_table_columns.cpp. Rust slices carry their length, so this mismatch can't be expressed.

6da784ac1: plan-cache accounting read a cached object after releasing the node write lock, while concurrent eviction could drop its last reference (src/sql/plan_cache/ob_plan_cache.cpp). A borrow tied to the lock guard would have rejected this.
6da784ac1: ObPsStmtInfo dereferenced ps_item_, which the prepare path can free first (src/sql/plan_cache/ob_ps_cache_callback.h). This is a dangling pointer across two owners.

bbfa2d543 (twin a44c7762d, #1166): virtual table row cells pointed into buffers owned by a local diagnose_info that was destroyed before the row was read (src/observer/virtual_table/ob_all_virtual_ha_diagnose.cpp). The borrow checker rejects a returned reference that outlives its owner.

dd899675c: fallback schema managers were allocated from rotating arenas that a concurrent refresh could reset, fixed by taking schema_refresh_mutex_; the same commit fixes the bound check `count() > MAX_PARALLEL_TASK` to `>=` (src/share/schema/ob_multi_version_schema_service.cpp). Rust helps with the arena race only if arena lifetimes are expressed as borrows; the off-by-one would remain a logic bug.

50652b1e9 and 5c2637685: PL interpreter per-call temporaries and SQL string copies were allocated on the long-lived exec allocator, so memory grew in long-running SQL (src/pl/ob_pl_interpreter.cpp). Rust's scope-based drop makes per-call cleanup the default, but a port that keeps a shared bump arena could repeat this.
survey.public_surface_tests: n/a as a code area; the relevant facts are how the test surface moves. At HEAD, tools/deploy/mysql_test has 283 .test / 305 .result files (largest suites: geometry 42, vector_index 22, fork_table 18, fts_index 15, subquery 11, expr 11), and tools/obtest has 509 .test / 555 .result. The mysql_test count went 600 (2026-03-09), 593 (2026-06-23), 503 (2026-08-22), 283 (HEAD). Tests that import internals have almost disappeared: unittest+mittest went from 2,030 files to 4 (the 678-file deletion is in 45cbbe9e1). In the last 30 days mysql_test got 5 ordinary commits (+176/-12 lines) and 1 bulk commit. Recent SQL fixes add cases there (e.g. 270b47ea9, 192aedaf6, 402f0e25b touch tools/deploy/mysql_test). Only the public-surface suite survives the churn, but it is itself being cut.
survey.units_of_work: For keeping a port in step with C++, the natural unit is the second-level directory: 18 under src/sql plus 36 loose files, 32 under src/storage plus 91 loose files, and 10 other top-level src modules. After 2026-08-25 the change feed arrives as GitHub PRs: 63 merged since then, with 35 commits touching src C/C++ in 30 days (32 ordinary, 3 bulk). A sync can therefore be run per PR. Parallel lines are separate units: 8 branches differ from HEAD by more than 1,000 code lines (feature/plugin, codex/namespace-worker-proxy-v20, feat/embedded-mode, feature/webassembly-shell, feature/webassembly, feature/assert, codex/palf-log-buffer-redesign, feature/rust), plus release/1.4.0 as a maintenance line.
open_questions: Is the internal oceanbase-lite repo still an active source of changes after 2026-08-25? Only its migrated MRs are visible (#1340, #1341, 4 open PRs), and the gitlab host can't be reached.

Where do [CP] commits come from exactly (OB master, 4_6_0_release, or another internal branch)? Only one body (6e53dd10f) names its source branch, and 3 of 6 sampled subjects were found in OB CE master.

Will seekdb resume taking OB mainline fixes, e.g. for vector index or hybrid search, which were the bulk of the 2025-12 [CP] wave? No stated policy was found in docs/, AGENTS.md, README* or the issues.

Which of the 18 open 'Remove ...' issues and in-flight PRs (#1356 obmalloc, #1427 ASSERT_COND, #1351 plugin, #1245 GIS to plugin) will land, and when? That decides whether the tree is settled enough to freeze for a port.
Will the large parallel lines (feature/plugin, feat/embedded-mode, namespace-worker, webassembly-shell) be merged into master before any port starts, or stay long-lived?
Is the 30-day rate (about 8K ordinary lines a month) representative? It covers only the first month after the switch to GitHub-only development and includes a quieter week (2026-W39).
Near-duplicate commits (the same change with different conflict resolution) are not caught by patch-id, so the 90- and 180-day ordinary figures still carry some double counting.

survey.what_it_is: This area is the allocation-failure policy of seekdb: which allocators can hand a NULL (or a memory-limit error) back to a caller in the default jemalloc build, and which of the roughly 4,700 `ret = OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED` sites guard a failure that can actually happen. It covers the ob_malloc/jemalloc glue and malloc hook, the obmalloc context allocators, the module budgets (ObBlockAllocMgr and the FIFO allocators), the SQL work-area manager, the TxShare throttle, the KV cache store, and the existing Rust crate rust/sql-nio.
survey.size_split: Hand-written C++ directly in scope: 129 files / 34,491 lines (src/oblib/lib/alloc 33 files / 8,436; src/oblib/lib/allocator 36 / 8,320; src/oblib/lib/resource 5 / 1,635; src/oblib/lib/rc 4 / 1,005; src/storage/throttle 9 / 1,811; src/storage/allocator 14 / 2,098; src/share/cache 22 / 8,356; SQL mem mgr + processor 4 / 2,685; sql/executor/ob_memory_tracker.* 2 / 145). Of these, 26 files / 8,490 lines are obmalloc-only (block_set, object_set, object_mgr, abit_set, ob_ctx_allocator, ob_context_allocator, memory_dump, alloc_struct, alloc_failed_reason, achunk_mgr, ob_resource_mgr, ob_allocator_v2, ob_page_manager), plus the malloc hook (malloc_hook.cpp + malloc_hook_extended.cpp, 674 lines). Generated: the error-code tables that define -4013/-4030/-4080/-11049/-7603 (src/share/ob_errno.cpp, src/share/ob_errno.h, src/oblib/lib/ob_errno.h, 18,824 lines total, 'DO NOT EDIT ... generated from ob_errno.def'; ob_errno.def is 1,914 lines). survey.summary: In the default build (bundled jemalloc on Linux and macOS without ASAN), ob_malloc, ob_realloc and ObMallocAllocator call je_malloc/je_realloc directly and ignore ObMemAttr. The per-context limits, the label accounting and the global limit, all of which live in the obmalloc ObMemoryMgr/ObCtxAllocator path, are never checked. The setters for the global limit have zero callers, so the only failure left under the general allocator is jemalloc itself returning NULL. The memory_limit parameter is documented as deprecated and ignored, memory_budget only sizes things, and no system_memory parameter exists. The real fail points are a short list of module budgets. The clog slice allocators (30% of budget) return -4013 at 5 log_engine.cpp sites. The replay budget (min 5%, 512MB) is turned into OB_EAGAIN back-pressure. The IO allocator budget ends in -4013 for request/result objects and in a retry-until-timeout for IO buffers. The KV cache store has a fixed budget that runs its own synchronous wash and then fails with -4013, and that error can reach a read through put_cache_block. The vector module limit returns NULL/-7603. Four more budgets use their own error codes: the query memory tracker (-11049), the memstore-full check on DML (-4030), the temp-file write buffer pool (OB_ALLOCATE_TMP_FILE_PAGE_FAILED), and SQL work areas, which spill to disk instead of failing. The TxShare throttle for tx-data and MDS only sleeps, and their ObBlockAllocMgr stays at INT64_MAX. About 14 FIFO allocators carry large fixed caps (128MB to 10GB) that are practically unreachable. By my scripted classification, roughly 40 of the 4,737 `ret = OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED` sites (under 1%) sit behind one of these budgets; the rest check a NULL from arenas or ob_malloc that only comes from jemalloc. No mysqltest .result/.test, init SQL or bindings test expects 4013/HY001 (or -4030/-11049/-4080/-7603) or sets a limit low enough to trigger one. Allocation-failure injection (errsim EN_4) exists only on the obmalloc path, and no script selects that backend, so the 4013 handling code is effectively untested. On Linux the malloc hook sends every libc allocation, and so every Rust allocation, to jemalloc; on macOS the jemalloc zone is promoted to the default zone. rust/sql-nio already works the way I recommend: no global_allocator, panic=abort, handle_alloc_error, and try_reserve only where a client or peer controls the size. Recommendation: abort on OOM, plus explicit typed budget checks at 8 named budget owners (clog, replay, IO allocator, KV cache store, vector module, query memory tracker, memstore-full check, temp-file write buffer pool), plus the existing spill protocol for SQL work areas and the sleep-only throttle. Fallible collections everywhere would carry over about 4,700 checks for a failure that does not occur in the default build.

claims.claim: With MALLOC_BACKEND unset and OB_HAVE_BUNDLED_JEMALLOC defined, the backend is jemalloc. survey.structure_call: This area does not call for a 1:1 translation. A 1:1 translation would turn about 4,700 `ret = OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED` checks and about 6,470 `OB_FAIL(push_back)` checks into fallible collections. In the default build nearly all of them guard a jemalloc NULL that does not come back, and allocation-failure injection cannot test them. The error model should be redesigned. General allocation aborts on failure (Rust's default, already used by sql-nio with panic=abort and handle_alloc_error). The code that can really run out gets explicit typed budget checks: clog, replay, the IO allocator, the KV cache store reservation, the vector module, the query memory tracker, the memstore-full check, and the temp-file write buffer pool. SQL work areas keep their spill protocol, and the throttle stays sleep-only. try_reserve is kept only where a client, peer or data controls the size, as sql-nio does today. Push-style calls that can fail for non-memory reasons (ObFixedArray capacity, deep-copy assign) stay Result-returning, but as capacity or copy errors, not OOM. The obmalloc backend (26 files, 8,490 lines) and the obmalloc branch of the malloc hook should not be translated. The large fixed FIFO caps (128MB to 10GB) become plain allocations, or bounded queues where the cap is really a queue bound. Files that force the call: src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_malloc.h, src/oblib/lib/alloc/ob_malloc_allocator.cpp, src/oblib/lib/alloc/malloc_hook.cpp, src/oblib/lib/resource/ob_resource_mgr.cpp, src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_block_alloc_mgr.h, src/logservice/ob_log_allocator.cpp, src/share/io/ob_io_struct.cpp, src/share/cache/ob_kvcache_store.cpp, src/storage/allocator/ob_vector_allocator.cpp, src/sql/executor/ob_memory_tracker.cpp.
hard_parts: The ObIAllocator trait object is the receiver at about 2,500 OOM sites (receiver names 'allocator'/'allocator_'/'alloc'/'get_allocator()'). Arenas that hand out memory tied to a query or statement lifetime (src/oblib/lib/allocator/page_arena.h, src/oblib/lib/rc/context.h) need a Rust arena design (lifetimes, or bump arenas with explicit reset) because allocator_api is unstable.

Lock-free slice and FIFO allocators built on hazard pointers and quiescent-state reclamation: src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_slice_alloc.h (541 lines), ob_vslice_alloc.h (294), ob_qsync.h, ob_hazard_ref.h, ob_retire_station.h. This is unsafe-heavy code, intrusive block headers included.
The memstore arena with reference-counted pages retired by quiescent state: src/storage/allocator/ob_fifo_arena.cpp (ObFifoArena::alloc/free, WaitQuiescent).

The KV cache store: a fixed budget reserved with CAS, a synchronous wash under wash_out_lock_, hazptr-protected handle scans and a qclock retire station (src/share/cache/ob_kvcache_store.cpp:849-1000).

One allocator shared across the language boundary. C++ and Rust must keep freeing each other's pointers through the same jemalloc. On Linux that works today only because src/oblib/lib/alloc/malloc_hook.cpp and malloc_hook_extended.cpp interpose libc symbols; on macOS it depends on zone promotion in src/observer/main.cpp:645-653. A Rust #[global_allocator] with a different jemalloc prefix would break cross-frees during a mixed period.

Per-context memory accounting (ObMemAttr ctx_id and label; TrackedAllocator headers in src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_malloc.h:222-359; MemoryUsageTracker resolvers in ob_malloc.cpp:195-211). Rust's GlobalAlloc receives no attributes, so accounting has to come from explicit allocator handles or a thread-local context.

Variadic-template throttle framework with macro-generated units: src/storage/throttle/ob_share_resource_throttle_tool.ipp and ob_throttle_unit.ipp (ACQUIRE_THROTTLE_UNIT, DEFINE_CUSTOM_FUNC_FOR_THROTTLE).

The vsag third-party C++ library allocates through ObVsagMemContext (src/storage/allocator/ob_vector_allocator.cpp). The vector budget check must stay reachable from C++ through FFI, and a NULL returned to vsag is handled inside vsag.
pain_instances: Retry loops on -4013 that spin waiting for memory that the default build never withholds: src/share/cache/ob_kvcache_store.cpp:405-407 and 642-644 (do/while around hazptr protect until the result is not OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED); src/storage/meta_mem/ob_storage_meta_mem_mgr.cpp:374-409 (retries up to 1000 times with 100ms sleeps); the same code duplicated in src/storage/meta_mem/ob_tablet_meta_mem_mgr.cpp:371-404; src/storage/throttle/ob_throttle_unit.ipp:236-248 (sleep 10ms and retry).
The obmalloc malloc hook's ob_malloc_retry loops forever until allocation succeeds (src/oblib/lib/alloc/malloc_hook.cpp:75-86), so every NULL check behind libc malloc is dead code on that path too.

Configuration knobs that do nothing in the default build: _storage_meta_memory_limit_percentage becomes set_ctx_limit (src/storage/meta_mem/ob_meta_memory_limit.h:28-35), and _ctx_memory_limit is applied by a duty task (src/observer/ob_server_duty_task.cpp:60-80). Neither limit is read on the jemalloc path. memory_limit is documented as ignored (ob_parameter_seed.ipp:81-84) but is still set and tested by the seekdb-bindings tests.

Dead limit plumbing: ObMallocAllocator::set_allocator_limit and set_allocator_hard_limit have zero callers (ob_malloc_allocator.cpp:172-196). The ObFixedSizeBlockAllocator template, with its -4080 path, has no users outside its header (src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_fixed_size_block_allocator.h:293-301).

ObRADatumStore::need_dump reads the ctx allocator's limit and hold (src/sql/engine/basic/ob_ra_datum_store.cpp:1233-1256). Under jemalloc the hold is never updated (update_hold is reached only from ObMemoryMgr::alloc_chunk/free_chunk, ob_resource_mgr.cpp:55-105), so its 80% trigger never fires.
Zero-size requests are reported as OOM: ob_malloc on the jemalloc path returns NULL and logs OB_ALLOCATE_MEMORY_FAILED for nbyte <= 0 (src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_malloc.h:118-125).

The 4013 handling paths cannot be exercised in the default build, because errsim EN_4 injection exists only in obmalloc (src/oblib/lib/alloc/ob_ctx_allocator.h:427, ob_context_allocator.h:454) and no tracked script sets MALLOC_BACKEND.
An out-of-date duplicate header: deps/oblib/src/lib/allocator/ob_jemalloc.h lacks the ENABLE_SANITY branches present in src/oblib/lib/allocator/ob_jemalloc.h (diff of the two files).
survey.public_surface_tests: None of the 861 .result or 793 .test files under tools/deploy/mysql_test expects -4013/HY001, -4030, -11049, -4080 or -7603, and none sets a memory limit low enough to trigger one (git grep, 0 hits). Memory-related public tests exercise sizing and spilling only: join_many_table.test and join_many_table_single_field.test set ob_sql_work_area_percentage to 100 and then 5 (the spill path); test_suite/fork_table/t/fork_table_vector.test and test_suite/vector_index (all_virtual_vector_index_info) set vector_memory_limit = 0 (automatic). test_suite/inner_table/r/mysql/all_virtual_sys_parameter_stat.result pins the parameter names (memory_budget, memory_limit, kvcache_memory_limit, memstore_memory_limit, vector_memory_limit, query_memory_limit_percentage, _ctx_memory_limit, _storage_meta_memory_limit_percentage, _pdml_thread_cache_size), so dropping or renaming a parameter breaks that result even though no behavior test depends on it. tools/deploy/init.sql (54 lines) and init_user.sql (6 lines) set no memory parameter. seekdb-bindings: 9 tracked test files. lib/tests/test_open_parameters.cc and test_parameter_persistence.cc set and read memory_limit (1G/10G) and expect the value to persist; none expects an OOM error. Only 2 C++ unit tests touch this area (deps/oblib/unittest/lib/alloc/test_jemalloc_hook.cpp, deps/oblib/unittest/lib/allocator/test_malloc_backend.cpp), and both import internals (ob_jemalloc.h, ob_malloc.h). Result: abort-on-OOM breaks no public-surface test.
survey.units_of_work: 1) The allocator glue: ob_malloc.h/.cpp, ob_jemalloc.h and the malloc hook, 2 hook files plus 3 glue files. This becomes one small unit that keeps a single jemalloc shared by C++ and Rust; no port of the obmalloc branch. 2) The obmalloc backend, 26 files / 8,490 lines: leave it out (keep the C++ while it exists, then delete). 3) General-purpose allocator primitives in src/oblib/lib/allocator (36 files): arenas, slice/vslice/FIFO allocators and the qsync/hazard helpers. The natural unit is one file group per allocator family, about 6 families: page_arena, FIFO, slice/vslice/small, concurrent/LF FIFO, hazard/qsync/retire, and block alloc mgr. 4) Budget owners, one unit each, each translated together with its explicit budget check: ObLogAllocator (src/logservice/ob_log_allocator.*), ObIOAllocator (src/share/io/ob_io_struct.cpp and ob_io_manager.cpp), ObKVCacheStore (src/share/cache/ob_kvcache_store.*), ObVectorAllocator (src/storage/allocator/ob_vector_allocator.*), ObMemTrackerGuard (src/sql/executor/ob_memory_tracker.*), the memstore-full check (src/storage/tx_storage/ob_memstore_freezer.cpp plus the ob_access_service.cpp call), ObTmpWriteBufferPool (src/storage/tmp_file/ob_tmp_file_write_buffer_pool.*), and the SQL work-area manager with its spill signal (src/sql/engine/ob_sql_memory_manager.* and ob_sql_mem_mgr_processor.*). That is 8 units. 5) The throttle framework (src/storage/throttle, 9 files) and the shared memory allocator manager (src/storage/allocator, 14 files): 2 units. Each of the roughly 4,700 OOM sites is not a unit of work. Under abort-on-OOM they disappear as part of translating their host files, so the rulebook entry is one mechanical rule ('NULL-from-allocator check: delete; allocation aborts') plus the named exceptions above.
open_questions: Whether any production deployment runs with vm.overcommit_memory=2 or a single request large enough to make je_malloc return NULL. That is the only case where abort-on-OOM would turn a query error into a process abort; it cannot be settled read-only.

Whether anyone runs MALLOC_BACKEND=obmalloc in production. If obmalloc must be kept, the ctx limits (META_OBJ_CTX_ID, _ctx_memory_limit) become real fail points again and join the list of named budgets.

Which allocator is behind the 6 allocator_-> sites in src/storage/blocksstable/ob_micro_block_cache.cpp (around lines 399-402, 500-503, 681-683, 697-699): the 4GB cache FIFO or a per-query unbounded ObFIFOAllocator.

Whether a -4013 from the KV cache reservation reaching a read through put_cache_block (ob_micro_block_cache.cpp:442-446) happens in practice, and whether the Rust design should fall back to an uncached copy instead of failing the read.

On macOS, whether allocations made before inner_main promotes the jemalloc zone (static constructors, early Rust code) end up freed through a different zone, and whether je_zone_register alone already makes jemalloc the default zone.
How vsag behaves when ObVsagMemContext::Allocate returns NULL after the vector limit is hit (a third-party library, not in this tree).
Whether ObStorageMetaMemMgr and ObTabletMetaMemMgr are both live; the files are near-duplicates, each with its own 4GB meta_cache_io allocator.

(2) The 26-file 'obmalloc-only' group is not all obmalloc-only. alloc_struct.h/.cpp defines ObLabel, ObMemAttr, ObMallocHookAttrGuard and ObUnmanagedMemoryStat, which every allocation site and the malloc hook use. ob_resource_mgr.cpp's ObMemoryMgr::alloc_cache_mb has a jemalloc branch that the KV cache calls on the default path (ob_kvcache_store.cpp:1150, 1163). (3) ob_context_allocator.h/.cpp in that group is not compiled at all (no source inventory lists the .cpp). verification.structure_call_check: I agree with the direction: abort on OOM for general allocation, explicit typed budget checks at the few real budget owners, and no 1:1 carry-over of ~4,700 NULL checks and ~6,470 push_back checks. The code supports it. On the default Linux/macOS build every general path ends in je_malloc (ob_malloc.h:118-125, ob_malloc_allocator.cpp:62-70, malloc_hook.cpp:161-165). Uncaught std::bad_alloc from operator new already terminates the process (malloc_hook_extended.cpp:215-231, only 5 catch sites). sql-nio already aborts on OOM. Even the obmalloc path has no enforced limit, because limit_bytes_ is written while hard_limit_bytes_ is what update_ctx_hold checks (ob_resource_mgr.cpp:157-165 vs 229-240). Four corrections are needed before this goes into the rulebook. (a) The IO allocator entry is backwards. Request and result objects retry until the IO timeout, and data buffers fail with -4013, because try_alloc_buf_until_timeout has no callers (ob_io_define.cpp:866, 1129, 1189; ob_io_manager.cpp:722-770). (b) The named list misses -4013 sources that are not allocator NULLs, which a 'delete the NULL check' rule would not cover and which must stay as typed errors: hash-partition depth in hash join (ob_hash_join_op.cpp:837-842, ob_hash_partitioning_infrastructure_op.h:1699-1700), KV cache mb-handle pool exhaustion (ob_kvcache_store.cpp:1029-1030), the IVF cache vector limit (ob_vector_index_ivf_cache_mgr.cpp:163-164) and vsag NO_ENOUGH_MEMORY (ob_vsag_adaptor.cpp:61-62). (c) The micro block cache's 4GB FIFO is a real budget with a 3-try sleep loop. It reaches reads through generic allocator references (ob_micro_block_cache.cpp:396-402, 1115-1118). (d) The recommendation only holds for builds with bundled jemalloc. Windows x64 and Android arm64 (build.sh:46-47), and Bazel non-sanity builds, default to obmalloc with no malloc hook. On Windows there is no overcommit, so abort-on-OOM turns a recoverable query error into a process abort. That needs an explicit decision, or a platform policy.

missed.point: Several supported build targets do not use jemalloc. Windows x64, Android arm64 and Bazel non-sanity builds have no bundled jemalloc, so their default backend is obmalloc with no malloc hook. On Windows, commit limits make NULL returns real, and Rust allocations go to the system heap rather than the C++ allocator. This limits 'NULL never comes back' and 'one shared jemalloc' to Linux and macOS CMake builds.

verification.overall: The survey's numbers can be trusted: every count I rechecked with a different method matched, except the sql-nio file total (23/8,448, not 24/8,464) and a few small tallies (ObBlockAllocMgr instances, FIFO sites, memory-tracker call sites). Most behavior claims also match the code, including the jemalloc routing, the unused global limit setters, the ignored memory_limit, the KV cache wash-then-fail, the throttle that only sleeps, the spill protocol, the malloc hook and zone promotion, and the empty public test surface. There are two real mechanism errors. The IO allocator semantics are reversed. The ctx-limit explanation is wrong, and the correct version (limits are not enforced on obmalloc either) makes the survey's case stronger. Its only mysqltest search for the bare code 4013 used git grep -E with \b, which does not work here. A -P recheck confirmed the conclusion, but that check was vacuous as run. The main gaps are scope, not accuracy. The analysis silently assumes the Linux/macOS CMake build and does not address Windows, Android and Bazel non-sanity, which default to obmalloc. The list of real fail points misses several non-allocator -4013 errors, and its site estimate is a lower bound. Its recommendation (abort on OOM plus explicit budget checks) is sound for the jemalloc builds and can go into the rulebook. First, the IO entry needs fixing, the logical -4013 errors need adding, and there needs to be a stated decision on non-jemalloc platforms.
